sentences.zh: 武十三王

translations.literal: Thirteen princes of Emperor Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Thirteen Princes of Emperor Wu.

sentences.zh: 武帝二十六男：楊元-{后}-生毗陵悼王軌、惠帝、秦獻王柬。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu had twenty-six sons: Empress Yang the First bore Prince Dao of Biling, Gui; Emperor Hui; and Prince Xian of Qin, Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Of Emperor Wu’s twenty-six sons, Empress Yang Yuan bore Prince Dao of Biling, Sima Gui; Emperor Hui; and Prince Xian of Qin, Sima Jian.

sentences.zh: 審美人生城陽懷王景、楚隱王瑋、長沙厲王乂。

translations.literal: Lady Shen the meiren bore Prince Huai of Chengyang, Jing; Prince Yin of Chu, Wei; and Prince Li of Changsha, Yi.
translations.idiomatic: The Lady of Meiren rank surnamed Shen bore Prince Huai of Chengyang, Sima Jing; Prince Yin of Chu, Sima Wei; and Prince Li of Changsha, Sima Yi.

sentences.zh: 徐才人生城陽殤王憲。

translations.literal: Lady Xu of cái rén rank bore Prince Shang of Chengyang, Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xu, a consort of talent rank, bore Prince Shang of Chengyang, Sima Xian.

sentences.zh: 匱才人生東海沖王祗。

translations.literal: Lady Gui of cái rén rank bore Prince Chong of the Eastern Sea, Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Kui, a consort of talent rank, bore Prince Chong of the Eastern Sea, Sima Zhi.

sentences.zh: 趙才人生始平哀王裕。

translations.literal: Lady Zhao of cái rén rank bore Prince Ai of Shiping, Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zhao, a consort of talent rank, bore Prince Ai of Shiping, Sima Yu.

sentences.zh: 趙美人生代哀王演。

translations.literal: Lady Zhao the meiren bore Prince Ai of Dai, Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zhao the meiren bore Prince Ai of Dai, Sima Yan.

sentences.zh: 李夫人生淮南忠壯王允、吳孝王晏。

translations.literal: Lady Li bore Prince Zhongzhuang of Huainan, Yun, and Prince Xiao of Wu, Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Li bore Prince Zhongzhuang of Huainan, Sima Yun, and Prince Xiao of Wu, Sima Yan.

sentences.zh: 嚴保林生新都懷王該。

translations.literal: Lady Yan the baolin bore Prince Huai of Xindu, Gai.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yan, styled baolin, bore Prince Huai of Xindu, Sima Gai.

sentences.zh: 陳美人生清河康王遐。

translations.literal: Lady Chen the meiren bore Prince Kang of Qinghe, Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Chen the meiren bore Prince Kang of Qinghe, Sima Xia.

sentences.zh: 諸姬生汝陰哀王謨。

translations.literal: Various concubines bore Prince Ai of Ruyin, Mo.
translations.idiomatic: Other ladies of the harem bore Prince Ai of Ruyin, Sima Mo.

sentences.zh: 程才人生成都王穎。

translations.literal: Lady Cheng of cái rén rank bore Prince of Chengdu, Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Cheng, a consort of talent rank, bore the Prince of Chengdu, Sima Ying.

sentences.zh: 王才人生孝懷帝。

translations.literal: Lady Wang of cái rén rank bore Emperor Xiaohuai.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wang, a consort of talent rank, bore Emperor Xiaohuai.

sentences.zh: 楊悼-{后}-生渤海殤王恢。

translations.literal: Empress Yang the Lamented bore Prince Shang of Bohai, Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Yang Dao bore Prince Shang of Bohai, Sima Hui.

sentences.zh: 餘八子不顯母氏，並早夭，又無封國及追諡，今並略之。

translations.literal: Of the remaining eight sons the mothers are not recorded; all died young, and they received no fiefs or posthumous titles; here they are all omitted.
translations.idiomatic: Eight other sons left no record of their mothers; they died in childhood without enfeoffment or posthumous honors, and are passed over here.

sentences.zh: 其瑋、乂、穎自有傳。

translations.literal: As for Wei, Yi, and Ying, they have their own biographies.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Wei, Sima Yi, and Sima Ying are treated in separate biographies.

translations.literal: The printed page inserts a column-break marker.
translations.idiomatic: Here the source layout inserts a column divider.

sentences.zh: 毗陵悼王軌

translations.literal: Prince Dao of Biling, Gui.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Dao of Biling, Sima Gui (subsection heading).

sentences.zh: =毗陵悼王軌，字正則，初拜騎都尉，年二歲而夭。

translations.literal: = Prince Dao of Biling, Gui, courtesy name Zhengze; he was first appointed Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and died at age two.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Gui, posthumously Prince Dao of Biling, bore the courtesy name Zhengze; his first appointment was Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, and he died at the age of two.

sentences.zh: ，追加封諡，以楚王瑋子義嗣。

translations.literal: Later a fief and posthumous title were added, and Yi, son of Prince Wei of Chu, was appointed heir.
translations.idiomatic: The court later added a fief and posthumous honors, and installed Yi, a son of Prince Wei of Chu, as his successor.

translations.literal: The printed page inserts a column-break marker.
translations.idiomatic: Column divider in the received typesetting.

sentences.zh: 秦獻王柬

translations.literal: Prince Xian of Qin, Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Jian, Prince Xian of Qin.

sentences.zh: =秦獻王柬，字弘度，沈敏有識量。

translations.literal: = Prince Xian of Qin, Jian, courtesy name Hongdu; he was deep, keen, and possessed judgment and capacity.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Jian, Prince Xian of Qin, whose courtesy name was Hongdu, was grave, astute, and measured in character.

sentences.zh: ，封汝南王。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Prince of Runan.
translations.idiomatic: He received the title of Prince of Runan.

sentences.zh: 咸甯初，徙封南陽王，拜左將軍、領右軍將軍、散騎常侍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Xianning era he was transferred to Prince of Nanyang, appointed General of the Left, concurrent General of the Right Army, and Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xianning he was moved to the Nanyang princedom and appointed General of the Left, acting General of the Right Army, and Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 武帝嘗幸宣武場，以三十六軍兵簿令不料校之，柬一省便擿脫謬，帝異之，于諸子中尤見寵愛。

translations.literal: Once when Emperor Wu visited the Xuanyang drill ground, he handed him the rosters of thirty-six armies to review without prior notice; Jian took one glance and picked out every error, and the emperor marveled at him and favored him above the other princes.
translations.idiomatic: On an imperial visit to the Xuanyang parade ground, Emperor Wu suddenly gave him the registers of thirty-six commands to audit; with a single reading Jian caught every mistake, and the emperor was so impressed that he doted on him more than on his other sons.

sentences.zh: 以左將軍居齊獻王故府，甚貴寵，為天下所屬目。

translations.literal: As General of the Left he dwelt in the former mansion of Prince Xian of Qi and enjoyed exceptional honor; all the realm watched him.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as General of the Left he occupied Prince Xian of Qi’s old residence, basking in rare favor and the gaze of the whole court.

sentences.zh: 性仁訥，無機辯之譽。

translations.literal: By nature he was kindly and slow of speech, and had no reputation for quick wit.
translations.idiomatic: He was humane and plain-spoken, and no one praised him for clever repartee.

sentences.zh: 太康十年，徙封于秦，邑八萬戶。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Taikang he was transferred to Qin with a fief of eighty thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In Taikang 10 he was reassigned to the Qin princedom with a household quota of eighty thousand.

sentences.zh: 于時諸王封中土者皆五萬戶，以柬與太子同產，故特加之。

translations.literal: At that time princes enfeoffed in the central plain each had fifty thousand households; because Jian shared the same mother as the heir apparent, he alone received an increase.
translations.idiomatic: Other princes with domains in the heartland held fifty thousand households; Jian alone was granted more because he was the crown prince’s full brother.

sentences.zh: 轉鎮西將軍、西戎校尉、假節，與楚、淮南王俱之國。

translations.literal: He was promoted General Who Guards the West, Colonel of the Western Rong, granted the credential, and went to his state together with the Princes of Chu and Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: He was rotated to General Who Guards the West and Colonel of the Western Rong, given a credential, and traveled to his kingdom alongside the Princes of Chu and Huainan.

sentences.zh: 及惠帝即位，來朝，拜驃騎將軍、開府儀同三司，加侍中、錄尚書事，進位大將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Hui ascended the throne, Jian came to court and was appointed Grand Marshal Who Gallops as if Flying, with office equal to the Three Excellencies, plus Palace Attendant, chief of the Masters of Writing, and advanced to Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Hui took the throne, Jian attended court and was named Grand Marshal Who Gallops as if Flying with ad hoc honors matching the Three Excellencies, then added Palace Attendant and supervisor of the Masters of Writing before being raised to Grand General.

sentences.zh: 時楊駿伏誅，柬既痛舅氏覆滅，甚有憂危之慮，屢述武帝旨，請還籓，而汝南王亮留柬輔政。

translations.literal: At the time Yang Jun had been executed; Jian grieved that his mother’s clan had been destroyed and felt acute anxiety, repeatedly citing Emperor Wu’s intentions and asking to return to his fief, but Prince of Runan Liang kept Jian at court to assist the government.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jun fell, Jian mourned the ruin of his maternal kin and lived in dread; he often invoked Emperor Wu’s wishes and begged to return to his domain, yet Prince of Runan Sima Liang kept him in the capital to help govern.

sentences.zh: 及亮與楚王瑋被誅，時人謂柬有先識。

translations.literal: After Liang and Prince Wei of Chu were put to death, people of the time said Jian had foresight.
translations.idiomatic: Once Sima Liang and Prince Wei of Chu had been executed, contemporaries credited Jian with prescience.

sentences.zh: 薨，時年三十，朝野痛惜之。

translations.literal: He died in the first year of Yuankang at the age of thirty; court and countryside mourned him bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Yuankang 1, aged thirty, to the grief of officials and commoners alike.

sentences.zh: 葬禮如齊獻文王攸故事，廟設軒懸之樂。

translations.literal: His funeral followed the precedent for Prince Xian of Qi, Prince Wen You, and the temple was granted the suspended-music honor.
translations.idiomatic: Burial rites matched those for Prince Xian of Qi, Sima You, and his shrine received the full “suspended instruments” music.

sentences.zh: 無子，以淮南王允子鬱為嗣，與允俱被害。

translations.literal: He had no son; Yu, son of Prince Zhongzhuang of Huainan, Yun, was appointed heir, and Yu perished together with Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Without a natural heir, he took Sima Yu, son of Prince Zhongzhuang of Huainan, as successor; Yu was killed together with his father.

sentences.zh: ，追諡曰悼。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongning he was posthumously titled Dao (Lamented).
translations.idiomatic: In Yongning 2 the court added the posthumous name Dao, “the Lamented.”

sentences.zh: 又以吳王晏子鄴嗣。

translations.literal: Ye, son of Prince of Wu Yan, was then appointed to succeed him.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Ye, son of Prince Yan of Wu, was next named heir.

sentences.zh: 懷帝崩，鄴入纂帝位，國絕。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaohuai died, Ye entered and usurped the throne; the line then ended.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Xiaohuai’s death, Ye seized the imperial seat and the princedom lapsed.

translations.literal: The printed page inserts a column-break marker.
translations.idiomatic: Column divider in the received text.

sentences.zh: 三王

translations.literal: Three princes.
translations.idiomatic: Three Princes.

sentences.zh: =城陽懷王景，字景度，出繼叔父城陽哀王兆後。

translations.literal: = Prince Huai of Chengyang, Jing, courtesy name Jingdu, was given in adoption to succeed his uncle Prince Ai of Chengyang, Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Jing, Prince Huai of Chengyang, courtesy name Jingdu, was posthumously transferred to continue Prince Ai of Chengyang, Sima Zhao’s line.

sentences.zh: 受封，六年薨。

translations.literal: He received his fief and died in the sixth year.
translations.idiomatic: He took his enfeoffment and died in the sixth year thereafter.

sentences.zh: 東海沖王祗，字敬度，五月受封。

translations.literal: Prince Chong of the Eastern Sea, Zhi, courtesy name Jingdu, received his fief in the fifth month.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Zhi, Prince Chong of the Eastern Sea, courtesy name Jingdu, was enfeoffed in the fifth month.

sentences.zh: 殤王薨，復以祗繼兆，其年薨，時年三歲。

translations.literal: When Prince Shang died, Zhi was again made to continue Zhao; that same year he died, aged three.
translations.idiomatic: After the Prince Shang died, Zhi was again placed in Zhao’s line; he died the same year at three.

sentences.zh: 始平哀王裕，字濬度，受封，其年薨，年七歲。

translations.literal: Prince Ai of Shiping, Yu, courtesy name Jundu, received his fief and died the same year at seven.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yu, Prince Ai of Shiping, courtesy name Jundu, was enfeoffed but died that same year at seven.

sentences.zh: 無子，以淮南王允子迪為嗣。

translations.literal: He had no son; Di, son of Prince Zhongzhuang of Huainan, was appointed heir.
translations.idiomatic: He left no heir, so Di, a son of Prince Zhongzhuang of Huainan, succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 太康十年，改封漢王，為趙王倫所害。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Taikang he was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Han and was killed by Prince Zhao Lun.
translations.idiomatic: In Taikang 10 his title was changed to Prince of Han, and Prince Zhao Sima Lun had him murdered.

translations.literal: The printed page inserts a column-break marker.
translations.idiomatic: Column divider in the received text.

sentences.zh: 淮南忠壯王允

translations.literal: Prince Zhongzhuang of Huainan, Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zhongzhuang of Huainan, Sima Yun (subsection heading).

sentences.zh: =淮南忠壯王允，字欽度，咸寧三年，封濮陽王，拜越騎校尉。

translations.literal: = Prince Zhongzhuang of Huainan, Yun, courtesy name Qindu; in the third year of Xianning he was enfeoffed Prince of Puyang and appointed Colonel of Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yun, Prince Zhongzhuang of Huainan, courtesy name Qindu, became Prince of Puyang in Xianning 3 and was named Colonel of Agile Cavalry.

sentences.zh: ，徙封淮南，仍之國，都督揚江二州諸軍事、鎮東大將軍、假節。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Huainan, proceeded to his state, superintended all military affairs of Yang and Jiang provinces, General Who Guards the East, and granted the credential.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to the Huainan princedom and went to his domain as commander of Yang and Jiang military affairs, General Who Guards the East, with a credential.

sentences.zh: 入朝。

translations.literal: He entered the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He came to court.

sentences.zh: 初，湣懷之廢，議者將立允為太弟。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Crown Prince Minhuai was deposed, deliberators had intended to establish Yun as grand heir.
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Minhuai was removed, some had wanted to install Yun as heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 會趙王倫廢賈后，詔遂以允為驃騎將軍、開府儀同三司、侍中，都督如故，領中護軍。

translations.literal: When Prince Zhao Lun deposed Empress Jia, an edict then appointed Yun Grand Marshal Who Gallops as if Flying with office equal to the Three Excellencies, Palace Attendant, with command as before, and concurrent Defender of the Center.
translations.idiomatic: Once Prince Zhao Lun cast out Empress Jia, an edict named Yun Grand Marshal Who Gallops as if Flying at Three Excellencies rank, Palace Attendant, keeping his previous command and adding Defender of the Center.

sentences.zh: 允性沈毅，宿衛將士皆敬服之。

translations.literal: Yun was by nature steady and resolute; the palace guards all respected him.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yun was grave and firm, and the household guards stood in awe of him.

sentences.zh: 倫既有篡逆志，允陰知之，稱疾不朝，密養死士，潛謀誅倫。

translations.literal: Lun already harbored usurpation; Yun secretly knew it, pleaded illness and skipped court, secretly fed bravos, and plotted to kill Lun.
translations.idiomatic: When Lun began aiming at the throne, Yun perceived it; he feigned sickness, stayed away from audience, and secretly raised desperate men to strike Lun.

sentences.zh: 倫甚憚之，轉為太尉，外示優祟，實奪其兵也。

translations.literal: Lun greatly feared him, transferred him to Grand Commandant, outwardly honoring him while stripping his troops.
translations.idiomatic: Lun dreaded him, shifted him to Grand Commandant, seeming to exalt him while actually taking away his soldiers.

sentences.zh: 允稱疾不拜。

translations.literal: Yun pleaded illness and refused the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Yun claimed illness and would not accept the post.

sentences.zh: 倫遣御史逼允，收官屬以下，劾乙太逆。

translations.literal: Lun sent an imperial clerk to pressure Yun, seized his subordinates, and impeached him for the capital crime of great treason (text reads 乙 for 以).
translations.idiomatic: Lun dispatched a censor to hound Yun, arrested his staff, and charged him with high treason.

sentences.zh: 允恚，視詔，乃孫秀手書也。

translations.literal: Yun, furious, looked at the edict and saw it was in Sun Xiu’s own hand.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Yun examined the supposed edict and found it handwritten by Sun Xiu.

sentences.zh: 大怒，便收御史，將斬之，御史走而獲免，斬其令史二人。

translations.literal: In great anger he seized the clerk and was about to execute him; the clerk fled and escaped death, but two clerks were beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: He seized the censor and meant to behead him; the man escaped, but Yun cut down two registry clerks.

sentences.zh: 厲色謂左右曰：「趙王欲破我家！

translations.literal: With a stern look he told those around him: “Prince Zhao intends to destroy my house!”
translations.idiomatic: He said sharply to his attendants, “Prince Zhao means to ruin our family!”

sentences.zh: 」遂率國兵及帳下七百人直出，大呼曰：「趙王反，我將攻之，佐淮南王者左袒。

translations.literal: He then led his state troops and seven hundred household retainers straight out, shouting: “Prince Zhao rebels; I am going to attack him—whoever sides with the Prince of Huainan, bare your left arm!”
translations.idiomatic: He marched out with his princely army and seven hundred personal followers, crying, “Prince Zhao rebels! I march against him—if you stand with the Prince of Huainan, strip your left shoulder!”

sentences.zh: 」於是歸之者甚眾。

translations.literal: At this very many rallied to him.
translations.idiomatic: A great crowd answered his call.

sentences.zh: 允將赴宮，尚書左丞輿閉東掖門，允不得入，遂圍相府。

translations.literal: Yun was about to enter the palace; the Palace Aid to the Left of the Secretariat, Wang Yu, closed the Eastern Ye Gate, so Yun could not enter and besieged the chancellor’s office instead.
translations.idiomatic: As Yun headed for the palace, Wang Yu, Palace Aid to the Left of the Secretariat, shut the Eastern Ye Gate; blocked from entry, Yun surrounded the ministerial mansion.

sentences.zh: 允所將兵，皆淮南奇才劍客也。

translations.literal: The troops Yun led were all Huainan swordsmen of extraordinary skill.
translations.idiomatic: Yun’s soldiers were Huainan’s finest swordsmen.

sentences.zh: 與戰，頻敗之，倫兵死者千餘人。

translations.literal: They fought repeatedly and defeated them; over a thousand of Lun’s men died.
translations.idiomatic: They engaged again and again and broke Lun’s ranks, killing more than a thousand of his troops.

sentences.zh: 太子左率陳徽勒東宮兵鼓噪于內以應，允結陳于承華門前，弓弩齊發，射倫，飛矢雨下。

translations.literal: Crown Prince’s Left Leader of Household Chen Hui drove the Eastern Palace troops to drum and shout within in support; Yun formed ranks before the Chenghua Gate and crossbows volleyed, shooting at Lun like a rain of arrows.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Hui, the crown prince’s left leader, roused Eastern Palace guards to cheer from inside; Yun drew up lines before Chenghua Gate and every bow fired, showering Lun with bolts.

sentences.zh: 主書司馬畦秘以身蔽倫，箭中其背而死。

translations.literal: Registrar Marshal Sui Mi of the Documents Bureau shielded Lun with his body; an arrow struck his back and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Sui Mi, registrar marshal of the Documents Bureau, threw himself in front of Lun and caught a bolt in the back that killed him.

sentences.zh: 倫官屬皆隱樹而立，每樹輒中數百箭，自辰至未。

translations.literal: Lun’s officials all hid behind trees; each tree took several hundred arrows from the hour chen to wei.
translations.idiomatic: Lun’s staff crouched behind trees, and every trunk caught hundreds of shafts from mid-morning past noon.

sentences.zh: 徽兄淮時為中書令，遣麾騶虞以解鬥。

translations.literal: Hui’s elder brother Huai was then Palace Secretary and sent out a banner with the sable to stop the fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Hui’s brother Chen Huai—then Palace Secretary—sent out the imperial escort bearing the sable pennant to break up the melee.

sentences.zh: 倫子虔為侍中，在門下省，密要壯士，約以富貴。

translations.literal: Lun’s son Qian was Palace Attendant in the Gate Office and secretly recruited stalwarts with promises of wealth and rank.
translations.idiomatic: Lun’s son Qian, serving as Palace Attendant under the Gate Bureau, secretly enlisted braves with pledges of riches.

sentences.zh: 於是遣司馬督護伏胤領騎四百從宮中出，舉空版，詐言有詔助淮南王允。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent Commandant Protector Fu Yin with four hundred horsemen out from the palace, raising an empty tablet and falsely claiming an edict to aid Prince Zhongzhuang of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered Fu Yin, commandant protector, to lead four hundred riders from the palace waving a blank board and pretending an edict supported Prince Zhongzhuang of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 允不之覺，開陳納之，下車受詔，為胤所害，時年二十九。

translations.literal: Yun did not perceive the ruse, opened his lines to admit them, stepped down to receive the edict, and Yin slew him; he was twenty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: Yun failed to see the trick, opened his formation, dismounted to hear the “edict,” and Yin cut him down; he was twenty-nine.

sentences.zh: 初，倫兵敗，皆相傳：「已擒倫矣。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Lun’s army was failing, word spread everywhere: “Lun has been captured.”
translations.idiomatic: At first, as Lun’s force faltered, rumor ran, “Lun is taken.”

sentences.zh: 」百姓大悅。

translations.literal: The common people were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The populace rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 既而聞允死，莫不歎息。

translations.literal: When they soon learned Yun had died, none could hold back a sigh.
translations.idiomatic: Learning soon afterward that Yun had fallen, everyone groaned in sorrow.

sentences.zh: 允三子皆被害，坐允夷滅者數千人。

translations.literal: All three of Yun’s sons were killed; several thousand persons connected to Yun were exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: Yun’s three sons died with him, and thousands linked to his household were wiped out.

sentences.zh: 及倫誅，齊王冏上表理允曰：「故淮南王允忠孝篤誠，憂國忘身，討亂奮發，幾於克捷。

translations.literal: After Lun was executed, Prince of Qi Jiong submitted a memorial vindicating Yun: “The late Prince Zhongzhuang of Huainan was utterly loyal and filial, forgot himself for the state, rose against rebellion, and nearly succeeded.”
translations.idiomatic: Once Lun fell, Prince of Qi Sima Jiong petitioned to clear Yun’s name: “The late Prince Zhongzhuang of Huainan was loyal and dutiful, risked everything for the realm, struck at usurpation, and almost prevailed.”

sentences.zh: 遭天凶運，奄至隕沒，逆黨進惡，並害三子，冤魂酷毒，莫不悲酸。

translations.literal: He met heaven’s cruel fortune and suddenly perished; the traitorous faction grew vicious and slew all three sons; wronged spirits in bitter torment left none unmoved.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven turned cruelly against him and cut him off; the usurpers’ clique then murdered his three boys, and the injustice wrung tears from every breast.

sentences.zh: 洎興義兵，淮南國人自相率領，眾過萬人，人懷慷愾，湣國統滅絕，發言流涕。

translations.literal: When righteous troops rose, the people of Huainan gathered on their own, more than ten thousand strong, each burning with rage; the line of Min was cut off, and they spoke through tears.
translations.idiomatic: When loyal armies rose, Huainan subjects rallied over ten thousand strong, hearts afire; with the Min succession extinguished, they wept as they spoke.

sentences.zh: 臣輒以息超繼允後，以尉存亡。

translations.literal: Your servant therefore places his son Chao in Yun’s line to comfort the living and the dead.”
translations.idiomatic: I therefore ask to post my son Chao to continue Yun’s line and bring peace to both worlds.”

sentences.zh: 」有詔改葬，賜以殊禮，追贈司徒。

translations.literal: An edict ordered reburial with extraordinary rites and posthumous advancement to Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: The throne commanded a new burial with exceptional honors and posthumously named him Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 冏敗，超被幽金墉城。

translations.literal: When Jiong fell, Chao was imprisoned at the Jinyong fortress.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiong’s defeat, Chao was locked in Jinyong.

sentences.zh: 後更以吳王晏子祥為嗣，拜散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Later Xiang, son of Prince of Wu Yan, was appointed successor and named Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Later Sima Xiang, son of Prince Yan of Wu, succeeded him and was appointed Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 洛京傾覆，為劉聰所害。

translations.literal: When Luoyang collapsed he was killed by Liu Cong.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital fell, Liu Cong executed him.

translations.literal: The printed page inserts a column-break marker.
translations.idiomatic: Column divider in the received text.

sentences.zh: 二王

translations.literal: Two princes.
translations.idiomatic: Two Princes.

sentences.zh: =代哀王演，字宏度，太康十年受封。

translations.literal: = Prince Ai of Dai, Yan, courtesy name Hongdu, received his fief in the tenth year of Taikang.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yan, Prince Ai of Dai, courtesy name Hongdu, was enfeoffed in Taikang 10.

sentences.zh: 少有廢疾，不之國，演常止于宮中。

translations.literal: From youth he had a crippling illness and did not go to his state; Yan always remained in the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Chronic infirmity kept him from his domain, and he stayed perpetually within the palace.

sentences.zh: 薨，無子，以成都王穎子廓為嗣，改封中都王，後與穎俱死。

translations.literal: He died without a son; Kuo, son of Prince of Chengdu Ying, was appointed heir, re-enfeoffed Prince of Zhongdu, and later died together with Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Childless, he was succeeded by Sima Kuo, son of Prince Ying of Chengdu, re-titled Prince of Zhongdu; Kuo later perished with Ying.

sentences.zh: 新都王該，字玄度，咸寧三年受封，薨，時年十二。

translations.literal: Prince of Xindu Gai, courtesy name Xuandu, was enfeoffed in the third year of Xianning and died at twelve.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Gai, Prince of Xindu, courtesy name Xuandu, received his title in Xianning 3 and died at twelve.

sentences.zh: 無子，國除。

translations.literal: He had no son; the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Without an heir, the princedom was struck.

translations.literal: The printed page inserts a column-break marker.
translations.idiomatic: Column divider in the received text.

sentences.zh: 清河康王遐

translations.literal: Prince Kang of Qinghe, Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Kang of Qinghe, Sima Xia (subsection heading).

sentences.zh: =清河康王遐，字深度，美容儀，有精彩，武帝愛之。

translations.literal: = Prince Kang of Qinghe, Xia, courtesy name Shendu; he had handsome features and striking spirit, and Emperor Wu loved him.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Xia, Prince Kang of Qinghe, courtesy name Shendu, was fine-looking and vivid in bearing, and Emperor Wu doted on him.

sentences.zh: 既受封，出繼叔父城陽哀王兆。

translations.literal: Once enfeoffed, he was given in adoption to succeed his uncle Prince Ai of Chengyang, Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: After his enfeoffment he was transferred to continue Prince Ai of Chengyang, Sima Zhao.

sentences.zh: ，封渤海郡，曆右將軍、散騎常侍、前將軍。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed with Bohai commandery and successively served as General of the Right, Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, and General of the Van.
translations.idiomatic: He received Bohai commandery and in turn held General of the Right, Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, and General of the Van.

sentences.zh: 元康初，進撫軍將軍，加侍中，遐長而懦弱，無所是非。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yuankang era he was promoted General Who Comforts the Army, added Palace Attendant; Xia grew up timid and weak and judged nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuankang he rose to General Who Comforts the Army with the added title of palace attendant, yet as an adult he remained timorous and never took a clear stand on anything.

sentences.zh: 性好內，不能接士大夫。

translations.literal: By nature he loved the inner quarters and could not mingle with gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: He preferred the harem to the company of officials and scholars.

sentences.zh: 及楚王瑋之舉兵也，使遐收衛瓘，而瓘故吏榮晦遂盡殺瓘子孫，遐不能禁，為世所尤。

translations.literal: When Prince Wei of Chu raised troops, he sent Xia to arrest Wei Guan, but Guan’s former clerk Rong Hui then slaughtered Guan’s sons and grandsons to the last, and Xia could not stop it; the age blamed him.
translations.idiomatic: During Prince Wei’s coup Xia was ordered to seize Wei Guan, yet Rong Hui, an old subordinate of Guan’s, massacred Guan’s entire posterity while Xia stood helpless, for which contemporaries condemned him.

sentences.zh: 永康元年薨，時年二十八。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongkang he died, aged twenty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Yongkang 1 at twenty-eight.

sentences.zh: 四子：覃、籥、銓、端。

translations.literal: Four sons: Tan, Yue, Quan, and Duan.
translations.idiomatic: He had four sons: Tan, Yue, Quan, and Duan.

sentences.zh: 覃嗣立。

translations.literal: Tan succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Tan inherited his title.

sentences.zh: 及沖太孫薨，齊王冏表曰：「東宮曠然，塚嗣莫繼。

translations.literal: When Grand Heir Chong died, Prince of Qi Jiong submitted a memorial: “The Eastern Palace stands empty; no heir continues the tomb-line.
translations.idiomatic: After the grand heir Chong passed away, Sima Jiong of Qi petitioned: “The heir’s residence gapes vacant, with no successor for the ancestral shrine.

sentences.zh: 天下大業，帝王神器，必建儲副，以固洪基。

translations.literal: The great enterprise of All under Heaven, the divine regalia of emperors and kings, requires an established heir apparent to secure the mighty foundation.
translations.idiomatic: The realm’s great work and the sacred instruments of rule demand a designated crown prince to shore up the dynasty’s base.

sentences.zh: 今者後宮未有孕育，不可庶幸將來而虛天緒，非祖宗之遺志，社稷之長計也。

translations.literal: Now the rear palace has produced no pregnancy; one cannot hope vainly for the future and leave the heavenly line empty—it is not the departed ancestors’ will nor a lasting plan for the altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: With no royal pregnancy in sight, we cannot idle away the succession on mere hope; leaving the imperial line barren betrays our forebears and imperils the state.

sentences.zh: 禮，兄弟之子猶子，故漢成無嗣，繼由定陶；

translations.literal: By rites a brother’s son is as a son; therefore when Han Cheng lacked heirs, succession came from Dingtao.
translations.idiomatic: The canon treats a nephew like a son: when Emperor Cheng of Han had no issue, the line continued through the Dingtao princely house.

sentences.zh: 孝和之絕，安以紹興。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiao He’s line was cut off, peace was restored through Emperor An.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor He of Han’s posterity failed, Emperor An carried the house forward.

sentences.zh: 此先王之令典，往代之成式也。

translations.literal: These are the august models of former kings and the settled precedents of past ages.
translations.idiomatic: Such are the great precedents of antiquity and the working pattern of earlier dynasties.

sentences.zh: 清河王覃神姿岐嶷，慧智早成，康王正妃周氏所生，先帝眾孫之中，於今為嫡。

translations.literal: Prince Tan of Qinghe shows a godlike mien and precocious wisdom; born of Princess Zhou, the lawful consort of Prince Kang, among the late emperor’s grandsons he is now the senior legitimate line.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Tan of Qinghe, born to Prince Kang’s principal consort Lady Zhou, stands out in precocious brilliance and, among the late emperor’s grandsons, holds the foremost legitimate claim.

sentences.zh: 昔薄姬賢明，文則承位。

translations.literal: In olden times Lady Bo was worthy and wise, and Wen thereby received the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient Lady Bo’s virtue won her son Emperor Wen the throne.

sentences.zh: 覃外祖恢世載名德，覃宜奉宗廟之重，統無窮之祚，以甯四海顒顒之望。

translations.literal: Tan's maternal grandfather Hui bears generations of famed virtue; Tan ought to shoulder the weight of the ancestral temples, inherit an unending fortune, and quiet the yearning hope of the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: With a maternal grandfather, Hui, long celebrated for integrity, Tan should take up the ancestral charge, secure boundless blessing, and satisfy what all within the seas expect.

sentences.zh: 覃兄弟雖並出紹，可簡令淑還為國胤，不替其嗣。

translations.literal: Although Tan’s brothers have all been given out in adoption, one may select a virtuous one to return as heir of the state without ending the succession.
translations.idiomatic: Even though his brothers were posted to other lines, a worthy among them may be brought back as dynastic heir so the succession is not broken.

sentences.zh: 輒諮大將軍穎及群公卿士，咸同大願。

translations.literal: Your servant has consulted Grand General Ying and the assembled dukes and ministers; all share this great wish.
translations.idiomatic: I have sounded out Grand General Ying and the high ministers, and every one concurs.

sentences.zh: 請具禮儀，擇日迎拜。

translations.literal: I ask that the full ritual be prepared and a day chosen for the investiture audience.
translations.idiomatic: Let the court ready the full ceremony and fix a day to welcome him as heir.

sentences.zh: 」遂立覃為皇太子。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon Tan was established as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: ” Tan was thereupon named crown prince.

sentences.zh: 既而河間王顒協遷大駕，表成都王穎為皇太弟，廢覃復為清河王。

translations.literal: Soon Prince of Hejian Yong jointly moved the imperial carriage and memorialized to make Prince of Chengdu Ying grand heir younger brother, deposed Tan, and restored him to Prince of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Then Sima Yong of Hejian, maneuvering the throne, recommended Sima Ying of Chengdu as grand heir younger brother, stripped Tan of the heirship, and returned him to the Qinghe princedom.

sentences.zh: 初，覃為清河世子，所佩金鈴欻生隱起如麻粟，祖母陳太妃以為不祥，毀而賣之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Tan was heir son of Qinghe, the golden bell he wore suddenly sprouted raised grains like hemp seeds; his grandmother, Grand Consort Chen, deemed it ill-omened, destroyed it, and sold it.
translations.idiomatic: While Tan was Qinghe heir apparent, the gilt bell at his belt erupted in tiny raised bumps like sesame; his grandmother, Grand Consort Chen, took it for a bad sign, smashed it, and sold the metal.

sentences.zh: 占者以金是晉行大興之祥，覃為皇胤，是其瑞也。

translations.literal: Soothsayers said gold betokened the Jin element’s great rise; Tan was imperial seed—this was its auspice.
translations.idiomatic: Diviners read the metal as an omen of Jin’s resurgence and Tan as the imperial scion—that was its lucky sign.

sentences.zh: 毀而賣之，象覃見廢不終之驗也。

translations.literal: Destroying and selling it mirrored the proof that Tan would be deposed and not reach his destiny.
translations.idiomatic: Breaking and selling it foreshadowed his later deposition and unfinished fate.

sentences.zh: 永嘉初，前北軍中候任城呂雍、度支校尉陳顏等謀立覃為太子，事覺，幽于金墉城。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongjia, former Central Army Inspector Lü Yong of Rencheng and Commissary Colonel Chen Yan and others plotted to set up Tan as crown prince; when it was discovered, he was immured in Jinyong fortress.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yongjia, Lü Yong of Rencheng, Chen Yan, and others schemed to make Tan crown prince; exposed, Tan was locked inside Jinyong.

sentences.zh: 未幾，被害，時年十四，葬以庶人禮。

translations.literal: Before long he was murdered, aged fourteen, and buried with commoner rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was killed soon after at fourteen and interred with a commoner’s ceremony.

sentences.zh: 籥初封新蔡王，覃薨，還封清河王。

translations.literal: Yue was first enfeoffed Prince of Xincai; when Tan died, he was transferred back to Prince of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Yue had first held Xincai; after Tan’s death his title reverted to Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 銓初封上庸王，懷帝即位，更封豫章王。

translations.literal: Quan was first Prince of Shangyong; when Emperor Xiaohuai ascended, he was re-enfeoffed Prince of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Quan began as Prince of Shangyong; under Emperor Xiaohuai he was moved to Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 二年，立為皇太子。

translations.literal: In the second year he was established as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the reign he became crown prince.

sentences.zh: 洛京傾覆，沒于劉聰。

translations.literal: When the Luoyang capital fell, he fell into Liu Cong’s hands.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang’s collapse left him a captive of Liu Cong.

sentences.zh: 端初封廣川王，銓之為皇太子也，轉封豫章，禮秩如皇子，拜散騎常侍、平南將軍、都督江州諸軍事、假節。

translations.literal: Duan was first Prince of Guangchuan; when Quan became crown prince, Duan was shifted to Yuzhang with ceremonial rank like an imperial son, appointed Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, General Who Pacifies the South, and commander of Jiang military affairs with credential.
translations.idiomatic: Originally Prince of Guangchuan, Duan was reassigned to Yuzhang when Quan took the heirship, given a prince’s honors, and named Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, General Who Pacifies the South, and Jiang theater commander with a credential.

sentences.zh: 當之國，會洛陽陷沒，端東奔苟晞于蒙。

translations.literal: About to proceed to his state, Luoyang fell; Duan fled east to Gou Xi at Meng.
translations.idiomatic: He was on his way to his fief when Luoyang was lost; he bolted east to join Gou Xi at Meng.

sentences.zh: 晞立為皇太子，七十日，為石勒所沒。

translations.literal: Xi set him up as crown prince; after seventy days Shi Le seized him.
translations.idiomatic: Gou Xi proclaimed him crown prince, but seventy days later Shi Le took him captive.

translations.literal: The source line marks a column break.
translations.idiomatic: Column divider in the received page.

sentences.zh: 汝陰哀王謨

translations.literal: Prince Ai of Ruyin, Mo.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ai of Ruyin, Sima Mo.

sentences.zh: =汝陰哀王謨，字令度，薨，時年十一。

translations.literal: = Prince Ai of Ruyin, Mo, courtesy name Lingdu; he died aged eleven.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Mo, Prince Ai of Ruyin, courtesy name Lingdu, died at eleven.

sentences.zh: 無後，國除。

translations.literal: He had no posterity; the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Without heirs, the princedom was abolished.

translations.literal: The source line marks a column break.
translations.idiomatic: Column divider in the received page.

sentences.zh: 吳孝王晏

translations.literal: Prince Xiao of Wu, Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiao of Wu, Sima Yan.

sentences.zh: =吳敬王晏，字平度，太康十年受封，食丹陽、吳興並吳三郡，曆射聲校尉、後軍將軍。

translations.literal: = Prince Jing of Wu, Yan, courtesy name Pingdu, was enfeoffed in the tenth year of Taikang with revenue from Danyang, Wuxing, and Wu commanderies, and successively held Colonel of Archers Who Shoot by Sound and General of the Rear Army.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yan—here titled Prince Jing of Wu, though listed above as Xiao—bore the courtesy name Pingdu, received his fief in Taikang 10 with income from Danyang, Wuxing, and Wu, and served as Colonel of Archers Who Shoot by Sound and then General of the Rear Army.

sentences.zh: 與兄淮南王允共攻趙王倫，允敗，收晏付廷尉，欲殺之。

translations.literal: Together with his elder brother Prince Zhongzhuang of Huainan, Yun, he attacked Prince Zhao Lun; when Yun failed, Yan was seized and handed to the Minister of Justice for execution.
translations.idiomatic: He joined his brother Sima Yun against Sima Lun; after Yun’s defeat Lun arrested Yan and sent him to the Minister of Justice intending execution.

sentences.zh: 傅祗於朝堂正色而爭，於是群官並諫，倫乃貶為賓徒縣王。

translations.literal: Fu Zhi argued sternly in the court hall, whereupon the assembled officials all remonstrated, and Lun degraded him to Prince of Bintu county.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zhi confronted Lun bluntly at court; the ministers joined in, and Lun reduced Yan to a county-level princedom at Bintu.

sentences.zh: 後徙封代王。

translations.literal: Later he was moved to Prince of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: He was later transferred to the Dai princedom.

sentences.zh: 倫誅，詔復晏本封，拜上軍大將軍、開府，加侍中。

translations.literal: When Lun was executed, an edict restored Yan’s original fief, appointed him Grand General of the Upper Army with ad hoc office, and added Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Lun’s fall brought an edict restoring Yan’s old title, naming him Grand General of the Upper Army with independent command, plus palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 長沙王乂、成都王穎之相攻也，乂以晏為前鋒都督，數交戰。

translations.literal: When Prince Li of Changsha, Yi, and Prince of Chengdu, Ying, attacked each other, Yi made Yan vanguard commander; they clashed repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: During the war between Sima Yi of Changsha and Sima Ying of Chengdu, Yi named Yan front commander, and they fought many rounds.

sentences.zh: 永嘉中，為太尉、太將軍。

translations.literal: In the Yongjia era he became Grand Commandant and Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yongjia he rose to Grand Commandant and Grand General.

sentences.zh: 晏為人恭願，才不及中人，于武帝諸子中最劣。

translations.literal: Yan was by nature respectful and docile; his talent did not reach middling ability and among Emperor Wu’s sons he was the least capable.
translations.idiomatic: Humble and obliging, he lacked even average ability and ranked weakest among Emperor Wu’s sons.

sentences.zh: 又少有風疾，視瞻不端，後轉增劇，不堪朝覲。

translations.literal: Moreover from youth he suffered wind illness; his gaze was unsteady, and later it worsened until he could not endure court audience.
translations.idiomatic: He also had a palsy from boyhood that left his eyes unsteady; it grew worse until he could no longer face court.

sentences.zh: 及洛京傾覆，晏亦遇害，時年三十一。

translations.literal: When the Luoyang capital overturned, Yan likewise met death, aged thirty-one.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang’s fall claimed him as well at thirty-one.

sentences.zh: 湣帝即位，追贈太保。

translations.literal: When Emperor Min ascended, he was posthumously advanced to Grand Protector.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Min later honored him posthumously as Grand Protector.

sentences.zh: 五子，長子不顯名，與晏同沒。

translations.literal: Five sons; the eldest’s name is not recorded; he perished together with Yan.
translations.idiomatic: He had five sons; the firstborn’s name is lost, and he died alongside Yan.

sentences.zh: 餘四子：祥、鄴、固、衍。

translations.literal: The remaining four sons: Xiang, Ye, Gu, and Yan.
translations.idiomatic: The other four were Xiang, Ye, Gu, and Yan.

sentences.zh: 祥嗣淮南王允。

translations.literal: Xiang succeeded Prince Zhongzhuang of Huainan, Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang continued Prince Yun of Huainan’s line.

sentences.zh: 鄴即湣帝。

translations.literal: Ye is Emperor Min.
translations.idiomatic: Ye became Emperor Min.

sentences.zh: 固初封漢王，改封濟南。

translations.literal: Gu was first Prince of Han, then changed to Prince of Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: Gu began as Prince of Han and was later shifted to Jinan.

sentences.zh: 衍初封新都王，改封濟陰，為散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Yan was first Prince of Xindu, then changed to Prince of Jiyin, and served as Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Yan held Xindu, then Jiyin, and served as Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 皆沒於賊。

translations.literal: All were lost to the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: All fell victim to the invaders.

translations.literal: The source line marks a column break.
translations.idiomatic: Column divider in the received page.

sentences.zh: 渤海殤王恢

translations.literal: Prince Shang of Bohai, Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Shang of Bohai, Sima Hui.

sentences.zh: =渤海殤王恢，字思度，薨，時年二歲，追加封諡。

translations.literal: = Prince Shang of Bohai, Hui, courtesy name Sidu; he died aged two, and a posthumous fief and title were added.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Hui, Prince Shang of Bohai, courtesy name Sidu, died at two; the court later added fief and posthumous honors.

sentences.zh: 元四王

translations.literal: Four princes of Emperor Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: The Four Princes of Yuan Di.

sentences.zh: 元帝六男：宮人荀氏生明帝及琅邪孝王裒。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan had six sons: Palace Lady Xun bore Emperor Ming and Prince Xiao of Langye, Pou.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Di fathered six sons: the palace lady of the Xun clan bore Emperor Ming and Sima Pou, Prince Xiao of Langye.

sentences.zh: 石婕妤生東海哀王沖。

translations.literal: Lady Shi the jieyu bore Prince Ai of the Eastern Sea, Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Shi at jieyu rank bore Sima Chong, Prince Ai of the Eastern Sea.

sentences.zh: 王才人生武陵威王晞。

translations.literal: Lady Wang of cái rén rank bore Prince Wei of Wuling, Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wang, a talent consort, bore Sima Xi, Prince Wei of Wuling.

sentences.zh: 鄭夫人生琅邪悼王煥及簡文帝。

translations.literal: Lady Zheng bore Prince Dao of Langye, Huan, and Emperor Jianwen.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zheng bore Sima Huan, Prince Dao of Langye, and Emperor Jianwen.

translations.literal: The source line marks a column break.
translations.idiomatic: Column divider in the received page.

sentences.zh: 琅邪孝王裒

translations.literal: Prince Xiao of Langye, Pou.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiao of Langye, Sima Pou.

sentences.zh: =琅邪孝王裒，字道成，母荀氏，以微賤入宮，元帝命虞妃養之。

translations.literal: = Prince Xiao of Langye, Pou, courtesy name Daocheng; his mother was Lady Xun, who entered the palace of low status, and Emperor Yuan ordered Consort Yu to raise him.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Pou, Prince Xiao of Langye, courtesy name Daocheng, was born to Lady Xun, a low-ranking entrant to the harem, and Yuan Di placed him under Consort Yu’s care.

sentences.zh: 裒初繼叔父長樂亭侯渾，後徙封宣城郡公，拜後將軍。

translations.literal: Pou first continued his uncle Marquis of Changle precinct, Hun, then was moved to Duke of Xuancheng commandery and appointed General of the Rear.
translations.idiomatic: He first succeeded his uncle Sima Hun as Marquis of Changle precinct, then became Duke of Xuancheng and General of the Rear.

sentences.zh: 及帝為晉王，有司奏立太子，帝以裒有成人之量，過於明帝，從容謂王導曰：「立子以德不以年。

translations.literal: When the emperor became Prince of Jin, the authorities memorialized to establish a crown prince; the emperor, because Pou possessed the capacity of an adult beyond Emperor Ming, said calmly to Wang Dao, “I establish a son by virtue, not by age.”
translations.idiomatic: Once Yuan Di took the title Prince of Jin, officials asked him to name an heir; deeming Pou more mature than the future Emperor Ming, he remarked to Wang Dao, “I choose the heir by character, not birth order.”

sentences.zh: 」導曰：「世子、宣城俱有朗雋之目，固當以年。

translations.literal: ” Dao replied, “The heir apparent and the Duke of Xuancheng both enjoy reputations for clarity; surely age should decide.”
translations.idiomatic: ” Wang Dao answered, “The heir apparent and the Duke of Xuancheng are both praised for brilliance; precedence should follow seniority.”

sentences.zh: 」於是太子位遂定。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon the crown prince’s place was settled.
translations.idiomatic: ” The heir was thus fixed.

sentences.zh: 更封裒琅邪，嗣恭王后，改食會稽、宣城邑五萬二千戶，拜散騎常侍、使持節、都督青徐兗三州諸軍事、車騎將軍，徵還京師。

translations.literal: Pou was re-enfeoffed in Langye to continue Prince Gong’s line, his revenue changed to Kuaiji and Xuancheng with fifty-two thousand households, and he was appointed Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, Bearer of the Credential, commander of Qing, Xu, and Yan military affairs, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and summoned back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Langye to continue Prince Gong’s line, he drew income from Kuaiji and Xuancheng totaling fifty-two thousand households, took Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and credential-bearing command over Qing, Xu, and Yan, became General of Chariots and Cavalry, and was recalled to court.

sentences.zh: 薨，年十八，贈車騎大將軍，加侍中。

translations.literal: He died at eighteen, posthumously honored General of Chariots and Cavalry, with Palace Attendant added.
translations.idiomatic: He died at eighteen and was posthumously named General of Chariots and Cavalry with the added title of palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 及妃山氏薨，祔葬，穆帝更贈裒太保。

translations.literal: When Princess Shan died, they were buried together; Emperor Mu later added posthumous Grand Protector to Pou.
translations.idiomatic: Burial followed Lady Shan in joint tomb; Emperor Mu later posthumously named him Grand Protector.

sentences.zh: 子哀王安國立，未逾年薨。

translations.literal: His son Prince Ai, Anguo, succeeded and died within the year.
translations.idiomatic: His son Sima Anguo, Prince Ai, succeeded but died before a full year had passed.

translations.literal: The source line marks a column break.
translations.idiomatic: Column divider in the received page.

sentences.zh: 東海哀王沖

translations.literal: Prince Ai of the Eastern Sea, Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ai of the Eastern Sea, Sima Chong.

sentences.zh: =東海哀王沖，字道讓。

translations.literal: = Prince Ai of the Eastern Sea, Chong, courtesy name Daorang.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Chong, Prince Ai of the Eastern Sea, bore the courtesy name Daorang.

sentences.zh: 元帝以東海王越世子毗沒于石勒，不知存亡，乃以沖繼毗後，稱東海世子，以毗陵郡增本封邑萬戶，又改食下邳、蘭陵，以越妃裴氏為太妃，拜長水校尉。

translations.literal: Because Emperor Yuan believed that the heir son Pi of Prince of Donghai Yue had been lost to Shi Le with fate unknown, he made Chong continue Pi’s line, styled him heir of Donghai, added Piling commandery to enlarge the original fief by ten thousand households, shifted revenue to Xiapi and Lanling, made Yue’s consort Lady Pei grand consort, and appointed Chong Colonel of the Long River.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Di thought Sima Pi, heir of Sima Yue’s Donghai line, had vanished in Shi Le’s hands, so he installed Chong as Pi’s successor, titled him Donghai heir, expanded the domain with Piling and later Xiapi and Lanling, elevated Lady Pei as grand consort of Donghai, and named Chong Colonel of the Long River.

sentences.zh: 高選僚佐，以沛國劉耽為司馬，潁川庾懌為功曹，吳郡顧和為主簿。

translations.literal: Subordinates were chosen with care: Liu Dan of Pei as marshal, Yu Yi of Yingchuan as merit assessor, Gu He of Wu commandery as chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He recruited distinguished staff: Liu Dan of Pei as marshal, Yu Yi of Yingchuan as merit evaluator, and Gu He of Wu as chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 永昌初，遷中軍將軍，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongchang he was promoted General of the Central Army and added Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yongchang he advanced to General of the Central Army with Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 及東海太妃薨，因發毗喪。

translations.literal: When the grand consort of Donghai died, he thereupon conducted mourning for Pi.
translations.idiomatic: The Donghai grand consort’s death let him begin funeral rites for Pi.

sentences.zh: 沖即王位，以滎陽益東海國，轉車騎將軍，徙驃騎將軍。

translations.literal: Chong assumed the princedom, added Xingyang to Donghai, rotated to General of Chariots and Cavalry, then transferred to Grand Marshal Who Gallops as if Flying.
translations.idiomatic: Upon taking the princedom he annexed Xingyang to Donghai, moved from General of Chariots and Cavalry to Grand Marshal Who Gallops as if Flying.

sentences.zh: 薨，年三十一，贈侍中、驃騎大將軍、儀同三司，無子。

translations.literal: He died at thirty-one, posthumously honored Palace Attendant, Grand Marshal Who Gallops as if Flying, and office equal to the Three Excellencies; he had no son.
translations.idiomatic: He died at thirty-one, honored posthumously as palace attendant and Grand Marshal Who Gallops as if Flying at Three Excellencies parity, and left no heir.

sentences.zh: 成帝臨崩，詔曰：「哀王無嗣，國統將絕，朕所哀怛。

translations.literal: As Emperor Cheng faced death, an edict said, “The Prince Ai line has no successor; the state inheritance is about to fail—this is what I mourn.”
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed Emperor Cheng issued an edict: “Prince Ai’s house lacks an heir; the succession is failing, and it grieves me.”

sentences.zh: 其以小晚生奕繼哀王為東海王。

translations.literal: Let the younger son Yi, born late, continue Prince Ai as Prince of Donghai.”
translations.idiomatic: Let Yi, the son born to him in his later years, succeed Prince Ai in Donghai.”

sentences.zh: 」以道遠，罷滎陽，更以臨川郡益東海。

translations.literal: ” Because of the distance, Xingyang was revoked and Linchuan commandery was added to Donghai instead.
translations.idiomatic: ” Xingyang was then stripped away because of the distance, and Linchuan was added to Donghai in its place.

sentences.zh: 及哀帝以琅邪王即尊位，徙奕為琅邪王，東海國闕，無嗣。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ai assumed the throne from the Langye princedom, Yi was moved to Langye prince, and Donghai lacked an heir.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ai’s accession from Langye promoted Yi to that title, leaving Donghai vacant.

sentences.zh: 奕後入纂大業，桓溫廢之，復為東海王，既而貶為海西公，東海國又闕嗣。

translations.literal: Yi later entered to assume the great enterprise; Huan Wen deposed him, restored him as Prince of Donghai, then degraded him to Duke of Haixi, and Donghai again lacked succession.
translations.idiomatic: Yi later took the throne until Huan Wen cast him down, briefly restored his Donghai title, then reduced him to Duke of Haixi, so Donghai once more had no heir.

sentences.zh: ，安帝詔以會稽忠王次子彥璋為東海王，繼哀王為曾孫，改食吳興郡。

translations.literal: Emperor An’s edict named Yanzhang, second son of Prince Zhong of Kuaiji, Prince of Donghai to continue Prince Ai as great-grandson, changing revenue to Wuxing commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor An then named Yanzhang, second son of Prince Zhong of Kuaiji, as Prince of Donghai to continue Chong’s line in the next generation, shifting his income to Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 為桓玄所害，國除。

translations.literal: He was killed by Huan Xuan and the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan executed him and abolished the fief.

translations.literal: The source line marks a column break.
translations.idiomatic: Column divider in the received page.

sentences.zh: 武陵威王晞

translations.literal: Prince Wei of Wuling, Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wei of Wuling, Sima Xi.

sentences.zh: =武陵威王晞，字道叔，出繼武陵王喆後，受封。

translations.literal: = Prince Wei of Wuling, Xi, courtesy name Daoshu, was given in adoption to continue Prince Zhe of Wuling and received his fief.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Xi, Prince Wei of Wuling, courtesy name Daoshu, was posthumously transferred to continue Prince Zhe of Wuling and took his enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 咸和初，拜散騎常侍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianhe he was appointed Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xianhe he became Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 後以湘東增武陵國，除左將軍，遷鎮軍將軍，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Later Xiangdong was added to the Wuling state; he was removed to General of the Left, promoted General Who Guards the Army, and added Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangdong was later merged into Wuling; he stepped up from General of the Left to General Who Guards the Army with Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 康帝即位，加侍中、特進。

translations.literal: When Emperor Kang ascended, Palace Attendant and Specially Advanced were added.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Kang added palace attendant and Specially Advanced.

sentences.zh: 建元初，領秘書監。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyuan he headed the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianyuan’s opening year he directed the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 穆帝即位，轉鎮軍大將軍，遷太宰。

translations.literal: When Emperor Mu ascended, he rotated to Grand General Who Guards the Army, then advanced to Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Mu he moved to Grand General Who Guards the Army and then Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 太和初，加羽葆鼓吹，入朝不趨，贊拜不名，劍履上殿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taihe, plumed canopy and drum escort were granted, he need not hasten in palace approaches, need not be named when hailed, and might wear sword and shoes in the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Taihe’s start brought plumed canopy escort, freedom from hurrying in the palace, exemption from having his name called at obeisance, and permission to wear sword and shoes on the dais.

sentences.zh: 固讓。

translations.literal: He firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: He steadfastly refused the honors.

sentences.zh: 晞無學術而有武幹，為桓溫所忌。

translations.literal: Xi lacked scholarly learning but possessed military talent, and Huan Wen feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Xi had little book learning yet real martial ability, which made Huan Wen wary.

sentences.zh: 及簡文帝即位，溫乃表晞曰：「晞體自皇極，故寵靈光世，不能率由王度，修己慎行，而聚納輕剽，苞藏亡命。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jianwen ascended, Wen memorialized against Xi: “Xi issues from the imperial trunk; therefore favor and numinous rank shine through the age, yet he cannot follow royal norms, cultivate himself, and watch his conduct; instead he gathers the reckless and shelters fugitives.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Jianwen took the throne, Huan Wen indicted Xi: “Born of the supreme line, he enjoys glory through the generations yet spurns princely discipline, neglects self-cultivation, and shelters ruffians and outlaws.

sentences.zh: 又息綜矜忍，虐加於人。

translations.literal: Moreover his son Zong is arrogant and cruel, inflicting cruelty on others.
translations.idiomatic: His heir Zong is haughty and pitiless, visiting cruelty on the people.

sentences.zh: 袁真叛逆，事相連染。

translations.literal: Yuan Zhen rebelled, and the affair implicated him by association.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zhen’s revolt tangled him in shared guilt.

sentences.zh: 頃自猜懼，將成亂階。

translations.literal: Lately he has grown suspicious and fearful, about to become a source of turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: Recently his paranoia has mounted until he verges on stirring rebellion.

sentences.zh: 請免晞官，以王歸籓，免其世子綜官，解子㻱散騎常侍。

translations.literal: I ask that Xi be dismissed from office, returned to his fief as a mere prince, his heir Zong stripped of rank, and his son Jin removed as Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.”
translations.idiomatic: Strip Xi of office and send him back to his domain, dismiss Zong from the heirship, and cashier Jin from his cavalier post.”

sentences.zh: 」㻱以梁王隨晞，晞既見黜，送馬八十五匹、三百人杖以歸溫。

translations.literal: ” Jin followed Prince Liang with Xi; after Xi’s demotion he sent eighty-five horses and three hundred staves to Wen.
translations.idiomatic: ” Prince Jin of Liang accompanied Xi into exile; once Xi fell, Jin forwarded eighty-five horses and three hundred staffs to Huan Wen.

sentences.zh: 溫又逼新蔡王晃使自誣與晞、綜及著作郎殷涓、太宰長史庾倩、掾曹秀、舍人劉彊等謀逆，遂收付廷尉，請誅之。

translations.literal: Wen further coerced Prince Huang of Xincai to confess falsely that he plotted treason with Xi, Zong, Editorial Director Yin Juan, Grand Preceptor’s senior clerk Yu Qian, aide Cao Xiu, and secretary Liu Qiang; they were then seized for the Minister of Justice with a request for execution.
translations.idiomatic: Wen also forced Prince Huang of Xincai to incriminate himself alongside Xi, Zong, Yin Juan, Yu Qian, Cao Xiu, and Liu Qiang; all were jailed pending execution.

sentences.zh: 簡文帝不許，溫於是奏徙新安郡，家屬悉從之，而族誅殷涓等，廢晃徙沖陽郡。

translations.literal: Emperor Jianwen forbade it; Wen therefore memorialized to exile them to Xin’an commandery, their families following, while Yin Juan’s clan was exterminated and Huang was deposed and moved to Chongyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Jianwen refused the death plea, so Wen banished the party to Xin’an with kin in tow, executed Yin Juan’s family, and demoted Huang to Chongyang.

sentences.zh: ，晞卒于新安，時年六十六。

translations.literal: Xi died in Xin’an, aged sixty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Xin’an at sixty-six.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝三日臨於西堂，詔曰：「感惟摧慟，便奉迎靈柩，並改移妃應氏及故世子梁王諸喪，家屬悉還。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu mourned three days in the western hall and issued an edict: “Grief overwhelms me; escort the bier at once, relocate the coffins of Consort Ying and the late heir Prince Liang of Liang, and return all kin.”
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowu kept three days’ vigil in the western hall, ordering the catafalque brought home along with Consort Ying’s remains and the late Prince Liang’s funeral, and every dependent recalled.

sentences.zh: 」復下詔曰：「故前武陵王體自皇極，克己思愆。

translations.literal: ” A further edict said: “The late Prince of Wuling sprang from the imperial trunk and restrained himself in pondering faults.”
translations.idiomatic: ” Another rescript added: “The former Prince of Wuling stemmed from the throne and disciplined himself in repentance.”

sentences.zh: 仰惟先朝仁宥之旨，豈可情禮靡寄！

translations.literal: Looking up to the late court’s intent of benevolent pardon, how can affection and rite find no resting place!
translations.idiomatic: Honoring the prior reign’s merciful purpose, we cannot leave devotion and ritual unhoused!

sentences.zh: 其追封新甯郡王，邑千戶。

translations.literal: Posthumously enfeoff him Prince of Xinning commandery with a thousand-household fief.”
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously create him Prince of Xinning with a thousand-household estate.”

sentences.zh: 」晞三子：綜、㻱、遵。

translations.literal: ” Xi had three sons: Zong, Jin, and Zun.
translations.idiomatic: ” Xi left three sons: Zong, Jin, and Zun.

sentences.zh: 以遵嗣。

translations.literal: Zun was made successor.
translations.idiomatic: Zun inherited the line.

sentences.zh: 追贈綜給事中，㻱散騎郎。

translations.literal: Zong was posthumously awarded Palace Secretary; Jin, Cavalier Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Zong was honored posthumously as palace secretary; Jin as cavalier gentleman.

sentences.zh: 十二年，追復晞武陵國，綜、㻱各復先官，㻱還繼梁國。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year his Wuling princedom was restored, Zong and Jin each regained former offices, and Jin returned to continue Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve years later Wuling was revived, Zong and Jin recovered their posts, and Jin resumed the Liang succession.

sentences.zh: 梁王㻱，字賢明，出繼梁王翹，官至永安太僕，與父晞俱廢。

translations.literal: Prince Liang Jin, courtesy name Xianming, was given in adoption to continue Prince Qiao of Liang, rose to Coachman of Yongan, and was deposed together with his father Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Jin, Prince of Liang, courtesy name Xianming, succeeded Prince Qiao of Liang, reached coachman of Yongan, and shared his father Xi’s fall.

sentences.zh: 薨，子和嗣。

translations.literal: He died; his son He succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: At his death his son He inherited.

sentences.zh: 太元中復國。

translations.literal: Mid-Taiyuan the state was restored.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taiyuan years the fief was revived.

sentences.zh: 薨，子珍之嗣。

translations.literal: He died; his son Zhenzhi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: He died; Zhenzhi followed.

sentences.zh: 桓玄篡位，國人孔樸奉珍之奔于壽陽。

translations.literal: When Huan Xuan seized the throne, a man of the princedom, Kong Pu, escorted Zhenzhi to flee to Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: Under Huan Xuan’s usurpation, Kong Pu of the household guided Zhenzhi to refuge in Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 桓玄敗，珍之歸朝廷。

translations.literal: When Huan Xuan was defeated, Zhenzhi returned to court.
translations.idiomatic: After Huan Xuan fell, Zhenzhi came back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 太將軍武陵王令曰：「梁王珍之理悟貞立，蒙險違難，撫義懷順，載奔闕庭。

translations.literal: The Grand General’s order from the Prince of Wuling stated: “Prince Liang Zhenzhi is principled and upright; braving danger and exile, he embraced duty and loyalty and hastened to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Wuling’s order as grand general read: “Zhenzhi of Liang stood firm in peril, kept faith through flight, and hurried to the throne.

sentences.zh: 值壽陽擾亂，在危克固，且可通直散騎郎。

translations.literal: With Shouyang in turmoil he held fast amid crisis; for now appoint him Acting Cavalier Gentleman.”
translations.idiomatic: Amid Shouyang’s chaos he stayed resolute; provisionally name him acting cavalier gentleman.”

sentences.zh: 」累遷遊擊將軍、左衛、太常。

translations.literal: ” He rose through General Who Roams and Strikes, Left Guard, and Grand Master of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: ” He advanced to General Who Roams and Strikes, then Left Guard, then Grand Master of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 劉裕伐姚泓，請為諮議參軍。

translations.literal: When Liu Yu campaigned against Yao Hong, Zhenzhi was invited as staff adviser.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu’s western campaign named him advisory counselor.

sentences.zh: 裕將弱王室，誣其罪害之。

translations.literal: Yu intended to enfeeble the royal house, fabricated crimes, and murdered him.
translations.idiomatic: Seeking to sap the Sima house, Liu Yu framed him and had him killed.

sentences.zh: 忠敬王遵，字茂遠。

translations.literal: Prince Zhongjing Zun, courtesy name Maoyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Zun, Prince Zhongjing, courtesy name Maoyuan.

sentences.zh: 初襲封新甯，時年十二，受拜流涕，哀感左右。

translations.literal: He first inherited Xinning at twelve, wept at the investiture, moving all beside him.
translations.idiomatic: Taking Xinning at twelve, he sobbed through the ceremony and stirred everyone present.

sentences.zh: 右將軍桓伊嘗詣遵，遵曰：「門何為通桓氏？

translations.literal: General of the Right Huan Yi once called on Zun; Zun asked, “Why open the gate to a Huan?”
translations.idiomatic: When General of the Right Huan Yi visited, Zun demanded, “Why admit someone surnamed Huan?”

sentences.zh: 」左右曰：「伊與桓溫疏宗，相見無嫌。

translations.literal: His attendants said, “Yi is only a distant cousin of Huan Wen; meeting him is harmless.”
translations.idiomatic: Attendants replied, “Yi is a remote kinsman of Huan Wen; receiving him is harmless.”

sentences.zh: 」遵曰：「我聞人姓木邊，便欲殺之，況諸桓乎！

translations.literal: Zun said, “I hear of a surname with ‘wood’ beside it and want to kill the man—how much more the whole Huan clan!”
translations.idiomatic: Zun shot back, “I itch to slay anyone whose name bears the wood radical—let alone every Huan!”

sentences.zh: 」由是少稱聰慧。

translations.literal: ” From this he was praised as clever while young.
translations.idiomatic: ” Hence people called him precocious.

sentences.zh: 及晞追復封武陵王，以遵嗣，歷位散騎常侍、秘書監、太常、中領軍。

translations.literal: When Xi’s Wuling title was restored, Zun succeeded him, serving as Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, Palace Library director, Grand Master of Ceremonies, and Defender of the Center.
translations.idiomatic: After Xi’s Wuling restoration Zun inherited the seat, holding cavalier attendant, palace librarian, ritual director, and central defender posts.

sentences.zh: 桓玄用事，拜金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Under Huan Xuan’s power he was named Grand Master with golden seal and purple ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: While Huan Xuan dominated, he received the gold-seal purple-ribbon grand master title.

sentences.zh: 玄篡，貶為彭澤侯，遣之國。

translations.literal: When Xuan usurped, Zun was demoted to Marquis of Pengze and sent to his fief.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan’s coup reduced him to Pengze marquis and dispatched him to his domain.

sentences.zh: 行次石頭，夜濤水入淮，船破，未得發。

translations.literal: Halting at Stone Citadel, a night surge poured into the Huai, wrecking the boat so he could not sail.
translations.idiomatic: Stopped at Stone Citadel, a nocturnal flood burst into the Huai and smashed his craft, blocking departure.

sentences.zh: 會義旗興，復還國第。

translations.literal: When the righteous banner rose, he returned to his capital residence.
translations.idiomatic: The loyalist uprising let him go back to his city mansion.

sentences.zh: 朝廷稱受密詔，使遵總攝萬機，加侍中、大將軍，移入東宮，內外畢敬。

translations.literal: The court claimed a secret edict naming Zun to oversee all affairs, added Palace Attendant and Grand General, moved him into the Eastern Palace, and everyone within and without paid him reverence.
translations.idiomatic: Courtiers cited a clandestine mandate entrusting Zun with every matter, piled on palace attendant and grand general, quartered him in the Eastern Palace, and won obeisance from the whole apparatus.

sentences.zh: 遷轉百官，稱制書；

translations.literal: Officials were rotated under rescripts styled “imperial directive.”
translations.idiomatic: Personnel shifts went out under documents labeled imperial directives.

sentences.zh: 又教稱令書。

translations.literal: His instructions were styled “princely commands.”
translations.idiomatic: His own orders were titled princely commands.

sentences.zh: 安帝反正，更拜太保，加班劍二十人。

translations.literal: When Emperor An was restored, Zun was reappointed Grand Protector with twenty guards bearing swords.
translations.idiomatic: An’s restoration reinstated him as grand protector with a twenty-man sword escort.

sentences.zh: 義熙四年薨，時年三十五，詔賜東園溫明神器，朝服一具，衣一襲，錢百萬，布千匹，策贈太傳，葬加殊禮。

translations.literal: He died in the fourth year of Yixi, aged thirty-five; the edict granted eastern-park warmming vessels, one court robe, one suit, a million cash, a thousand bolts of cloth, posthumous Grand Tutor, and burial with extraordinary honors.
translations.idiomatic: He died Yixi 4 at thirty-five, receiving eastern-park mortuary gear, court dress, cash, silk, posthumous grand tutor, and a state funeral.

sentences.zh: 子定王季度立，拜散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: His son Prince Ding Jidu succeeded, appointed Gentleman Cavalier Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ding Jidu followed, named gentleman cavalier attendant.

sentences.zh: 薨，子球之立。

translations.literal: He died; Qiuzhi succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: He died; Qiuzhi inherited.

sentences.zh: 宋興，國除。

translations.literal: When the Song rose, the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The Liu-Song founding ended the fief.

translations.literal: The source line marks a column break.
translations.idiomatic: Column divider in the received page.

sentences.zh: 琅邪悼王煥

translations.literal: Prince Dao of Langye, Huan.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Dao of Langye, Sima Huan.

sentences.zh: =琅邪悼王煥，字耀祖。

translations.literal: = Prince Dao of Langye, Huan, courtesy name Yaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Huan, Prince Dao of Langye, courtesy name Yaozu.

sentences.zh: 母有寵，元帝特所鍾愛。

translations.literal: His mother enjoyed favor, and Emperor Yuan cherished him especially.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was a favorite, and Yuan Di loved him above others.

sentences.zh: 初繼帝弟長樂亭侯渾，後封顯義亭侯。

translations.literal: He first continued his imperial younger brother Marquis of Changle precinct, Hun, and was later enfeoffed Marquis of Xianyi precinct.
translations.idiomatic: He first succeeded his brother Sima Hun as Marquis of Changle precinct, then became Marquis of Xianyi.

sentences.zh: 尚書令刁協奏：「昔魏臨淄侯以邢顒為家丞，劉楨為庶子。

translations.literal: Director of the Masters of Writing Diao Xie memorialized: “Formerly Wei’s Marquis of Linzi appointed Xing Yong as household aide and Liu Zhen as bastard son’s tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Diao Xie, director of the Masters of Writing, wrote: “The Wei Prince of Linzi once named Xing Yong household steward and Liu Zhen tutor to the bastard heir.

sentences.zh: 今侯幼弱，宜選明德。

translations.literal: Now the marquis is young and weak; one should select bright virtue.”
translations.idiomatic: Today the marquis is a child; choose worthy mentors.”

sentences.zh: 」帝令曰：「臨淄萬戶封，又植少有美才，能同游田蘇者。

translations.literal: ” The emperor’s order said, “Linzi held a ten-thousand-household fief, and Zhi in youth had fine talent, companions fit to roam fields with Su.
translations.idiomatic: ” Yuan Di replied, “Linzi’s ten-thousand-household domain and Zhi’s youthful genius drew peers who could hunt and farm beside Su.

sentences.zh: 今晚生矇弱，何論於此！

translations.literal: This late-born child is ignorant and frail—why speak of that!
translations.idiomatic: This infant is dull and delicate—why raise such comparisons!

sentences.zh: 間封此兒，不以寵稚子也。

translations.literal: I casually enfeoff this boy, not to pamper a youngest son.
translations.idiomatic: I grant him a fief in passing, not to spoil a baby prince.

sentences.zh: 亡弟當應繼嗣，不獲已耳。

translations.literal: A deceased younger brother should have received the succession; I had no choice.
translations.idiomatic: My late brother ought to have inherited; this was unavoidable.

sentences.zh: 家丞、庶子，足以攝祠祭而已，豈宜屈賢才以受無用乎！

translations.literal: Household aide and bastard tutor suffice to oversee sacrifices—why waste worthy men on useless posts!”
translations.idiomatic: Steward and tutor are enough to mind the offerings—why press talent into empty sinecures!”

sentences.zh: 」及煥疾篤，帝為之撤膳，乃下詔封為琅邪王，嗣恭王後，俄而薨，年二歲。

translations.literal: ” When Huan fell gravely ill, the emperor withdrew his own meals for him, then issued an edict enfeoffing him Prince of Langye to continue Prince Gong’s line; soon he died, aged two.
translations.idiomatic: ” As Huan sickened, the emperor fasted in sympathy, then created him Prince of Langye continuing Prince Gong; he died almost at once, aged two.

sentences.zh: 帝悼念無已，將葬，以煥既封列國，加以成人之禮，詔立凶門柏曆，備吉凶儀服，營起陵園，功役甚眾。

translations.literal: The emperor’s grief knew no end; preparing burial, because Huan had been enfeoffed a full principality, he applied adult rites, ordering death-gate cypress sheds, full lucky and unlucky vestments, and a mausoleum—labor conscripts were vast.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning without measure, the court treated the toddler like a mature prince: death portals, cypress sheds, full regalia, and a tomb project that drafted huge labor.

sentences.zh: 琅邪國右常侍會稽孫霄上疏諫曰：

translations.literal: Right attendant of Langye, Sun Xiao of Kuaiji, submitted a remonstrating memorial:
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xiao of Kuaiji, right attendant of Langye, offered a critical memorial—

sentences.zh: 表寢不報。

translations.literal: The memorial was shelved without reply.
translations.idiomatic: —but it never received answer.

sentences.zh: 永昌元年，立煥母弟昱為琅邪王，即簡文帝也。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongchang, Huan’s younger brother by the same mother, Yu, was established Prince of Langye—this is Emperor Jianwen.
translations.idiomatic: Yongchang 1 raised Yu, Huan’s full brother, as Prince of Langye, the future Emperor Jianwen.

sentences.zh: 咸和二年，徙封會稽，以康帝為琅邪王。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianhe he was moved to Kuaiji and Emperor Kang became Prince of Langye.
translations.idiomatic: Xianhe 2 shifted him to Kuaiji while Emperor Kang took the Langye title.

sentences.zh: 康帝即位，哀帝為琅邪王。

translations.literal: When Emperor Kang ascended, Emperor Ai was Prince of Langye.
translations.idiomatic: Kang’s accession left Ai as Prince of Langye.

sentences.zh: 哀帝即位，廢帝為琅邪王。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ai ascended, Emperor Fei was Prince of Langye.
translations.idiomatic: Ai’s accession made Fei Prince of Langye.

sentences.zh: 廢帝即位，又以簡文帝攝行琅邪王國祀。

translations.literal: When Emperor Fei ascended, Emperor Jianwen again acted as celebrant for the Langye princedom.
translations.idiomatic: Fei’s rise had Jianwen once more oversee Langye sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 簡文登阼，國遂無嗣。

translations.literal: When Jianwen mounted the throne, the princedom lacked an heir.
translations.idiomatic: Jianwen’s enthronement left Langye without a successor.

sentences.zh: 帝臨崩，封少子道子為琅邪王。

translations.literal: Facing death, the emperor enfeoffed his youngest son Daozi as Prince of Langye.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed he named Daozi, his youngest, Prince of Langye.

sentences.zh: ，道子為會稽王，更以恭帝為琅邪王。

translations.literal: Daozi became Prince of Kuaiji, and Emperor Gong was then made Prince of Langye.
translations.idiomatic: Daozi moved to Kuaiji, and Emperor Gong received Langye.

sentences.zh: 恭帝即位，於是琅邪國除。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gong ascended, the Langye princedom was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Gong’s accession ended the Langye line.

sentences.zh: 簡文三子

translations.literal: Three sons of Emperor Jianwen.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Sons of Jianwen.

sentences.zh: 簡文帝七子：王皇后生會稽思世子道生、皇子俞生。

translations.literal: Emperor Jianwen had seven sons: Empress Wang bore Kuaiji’s posthumous heir Daosheng and Prince Yusheng.
translations.idiomatic: Jianwen fathered seven sons: Empress Wang bore Daosheng, posthumous heir of Kuaiji, and Prince Yusheng.

sentences.zh: 胡淑儀生臨川獻王郁、皇子朱生。

translations.literal: Lady Hu the shuyi bore Prince Xian of Linchuan, Yu, and Prince Zhusheng.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Hu, a shuyi, bore Prince Yu of Linchuan and Prince Zhusheng.

sentences.zh: 王淑儀生皇子天流。

translations.literal: Lady Wang the shuyi bore Prince Tianliu.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wang the shuyi bore Prince Tianliu.

sentences.zh: 李夫人生孝武帝、會稽文孝王道子。

translations.literal: Lady Li bore Emperor Xiaowu and Prince Wenxiao of Kuaiji, Daozi.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Li bore Emperor Xiaowu and Daozi, Prince Wenxiao of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 俞生、朱生、天流並早夭，今並略之。

translations.literal: Yusheng, Zhusheng, and Tianliu all died young; here they are omitted.
translations.idiomatic: Yusheng, Zhusheng, and Tianliu perished in infancy and are passed over.

translations.literal: The source line marks a column break.
translations.idiomatic: Column divider in the received page.

sentences.zh: 會稽思世子道生

translations.literal: Kuaiji’s posthumous heir Daosheng.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous heir Daosheng of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: =會稽思世子道生，字延長。

translations.literal: = Kuaiji’s posthumous heir Daosheng, courtesy name Yanchang.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Daosheng, posthumous heir of Kuaiji, courtesy name Yanchang.

sentences.zh: 帝為會稽王，立道生為世子，拜散騎侍郎、給事中。

translations.literal: When the emperor was Prince of Kuaiji, he established Daosheng as heir son, appointing him Gentleman Cavalier Attendant and Palace Writer.
translations.idiomatic: While still Prince of Kuaiji, Jianwen named Daosheng heir and gave him gentleman cavalier attendant and palace writer.

sentences.zh: 性疏躁，不修行業，多失禮度，竟以幽廢而卒，時年二十四，無後。

translations.literal: By nature he was careless and rash, cultivated no discipline, often breached ritual bounds, and ended confined and deposed, dying at twenty-four without posterity.
translations.idiomatic: Impulsive and negligent, he flouted decorum until he was imprisoned and cast aside, dying childless at twenty-four.

sentences.zh: 及孝武帝即位，嘗晝日見道生及臨川獻王郁，鬱曰：「大郎饑乏辛苦。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu ascended, he once saw Daosheng and Prince Xian of Linchuan, Yu, in broad daylight; Yu said, “Eldest brother, you hunger and suffer.”
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowu once saw Daosheng and Prince Yu of Linchuan in daylight vision; Yu murmured, “Eldest brother, you starve in hardship.”

sentences.zh: 」言竟不見。

translations.literal: ” The words ended and they vanished.
translations.idiomatic: ” The phantoms faded as he finished.

sentences.zh: 帝傷感，因以西陽王錄玄孫珣之為後。

translations.literal: The emperor grieved and therefore took Xunzhi, a descendant of the Xiyang princely line, as heir.
translations.idiomatic: Moved to sorrow, he adopted Xunzhi from the Xiyang house as successor.

sentences.zh: 珣之曆吳興太守。

translations.literal: Xunzhi served as governor of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Xunzhi governed Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 劉裕之伐關中，以為諮議參軍。

translations.literal: When Liu Yu campaigned into Guanzhong, Xunzhi was named staff adviser.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu’s Guanzhong expedition appointed him counselor.

sentences.zh: 時帝道方謝，珣之為宗室之美，與梁王珍之俱被害。

translations.literal: As the imperial way waned, Xunzhi, finest of the blood, was murdered together with Prince Liang Zhenzhi.
translations.idiomatic: With the dynasty failing, Xunzhi, jewel of the clan, died beside Prince Zhenzhi of Liang.

translations.literal: The source line marks a column break.
translations.idiomatic: Column divider in the received page.

sentences.zh: 臨川獻王鬱

translations.literal: Prince Xian of Linchuan, Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xian of Linchuan, Sima Yu.

sentences.zh: =臨川獻王鬱，字深仁，幼而敏慧。

translations.literal: = Prince Xian of Linchuan, Yu, courtesy name Shenren; in youth he was quick and clever.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yu, Prince Xian of Linchuan, courtesy name Shenren, showed precocious wit.

sentences.zh: 道生初以無禮失旨，鬱數勸以敬慎之道。
