translations.literal: When Daosheng first lost favor through rudeness, Yu repeatedly urged reverent caution.
translations.idiomatic: As Daosheng forfeited standing through discourtesy, Yu counseled humility again and again.

sentences.zh: 道生不納，鬱為之流涕，簡文帝深器異之。

translations.literal: Daosheng would not listen; Yu wept for him, and Emperor Jianwen prized Yu highly.
translations.idiomatic: Daosheng ignored him; Yu wept, and Jianwen esteemed him deeply.

sentences.zh: 年十七而薨。

translations.literal: He died at seventeen.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventeen.

sentences.zh: 久之，追諡獻世子。

translations.literal: Long afterward he was posthumously titled heir son Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Years later he received posthumous heir title Xian.

sentences.zh: 甯康初，贈左將軍，加散騎常侍，追封郡王，以武陵威王曾孫寶為嗣，追尊其母胡淑儀為臨川太妃。

translations.literal: Early in Ningkang he was gifted General of the Left, added Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, posthumously created prince of a commandery, with Bao, great-great-grandson of Prince Wei of Wuling, as successor; his mother Lady Hu was honored Grand Consort of Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Ningkang’s opening brought posthumous General of the Left, cavalier attendant, and princely enfeoffment; Bao, a descendant of Prince Xi of Wuling, continued his line, and Lady Hu became grand consort of Linchuan.

sentences.zh: 寶字弘文，曆秘書監、太常、左將軍、散騎常侍、護軍將軍。

translations.literal: Bao, courtesy name Hongwen, served as palace librarian, Grand Master of Ceremonies, General of the Left, Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, and Defender of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Bao, courtesy name Hongwen, held librarian, ritual director, General of the Left, cavalier attendant, and army defender posts.

sentences.zh: 宋興，以為金紫光祿大夫，降為西豐侯，食邑千戶。

translations.literal: When the Song rose, he was named Grand Master with golden seal and purple ribbon, reduced to Marquis of Xifeng with a thousand-household fief.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liu Yu’s rise he kept a nominal grand master title but was demoted to marquis of Xifeng at one thousand households.

translations.literal: The source line marks a column break.
translations.idiomatic: Column divider in the received page.

sentences.zh: 會稽文孝王道子

translations.literal: Prince Wenxiao of Kuaiji, Daozi.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wenxiao of Kuaiji, Sima Daozi.

sentences.zh: =會稽文孝王道子，字道子。

translations.literal: = Prince Wenxiao of Kuaiji, Daozi, courtesy name Daozi.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Daozi, Prince Wenxiao of Kuaiji, whose style duplicated his name as Daozi.

sentences.zh: 出後琅邪孝王，少以清澹為謝安所稱。

translations.literal: He was posthumously transferred to continue Prince Xiao of Langye and in youth was praised by Xie An for quiet simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: Adopted into Prince Pou’s Langye line, he won Xie An’s esteem in boyhood for serene detachment.

sentences.zh: 年十歲，封琅邪王，食邑一萬七千六百五十一戶，攝會稽國五萬九千一百四十戶。

translations.literal: At ten he was enfeoffed Prince of Langye with seventeen thousand six hundred fifty-one households and administered Kuaiji’s fifty-nine thousand one hundred forty households.
translations.idiomatic: At ten he became Prince of Langye with revenue from 17,651 households while overseeing Kuaiji’s 59,140.

sentences.zh: 太元初，拜散騎常侍、中軍將軍，進驃騎將軍。

translations.literal: Early in Taiyuan he was appointed Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, General of the Central Army, and advanced to Grand Marshal Who Gallops as if Flying.
translations.idiomatic: Taiyuan’s opening years brought cavalier attendant, central army command, then grand marshal who gallops as if flying.

sentences.zh: 後公卿奏：「道子親賢莫二，宜正位司徒。

translations.literal: Later the dukes memorialized: “Daozi’s kinship and worth are unmatched; he should take the Minister of Education seat.”
translations.idiomatic: High ministers urged: “No one matches Daozi in royal closeness and virtue; make him minister of education.”

sentences.zh: 」固讓不拜。

translations.literal: ” He firmly declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: ” He refused the appointment outright.

sentences.zh: 使隸尚書六條事，尋加開府，領司徒。

translations.literal: He was ordered to supervise the six articles of the Masters of Writing, soon added ad hoc office, and headed the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He oversaw the six Masters of Writing portfolios, gained independent command, and served as minister of education.

sentences.zh: 及謝安薨，詔曰：「新喪哲輔，華戎未一，自非明賢懋德，莫能綏禦內外。

translations.literal: When Xie An died, an edict said, “We have newly lost a wise pillar; Chinese and barbarians are not yet one—without enlightened worthies of thick virtue none can pacify within and without.”
translations.idiomatic: Xie An’s death brought a rescript mourning a fallen pillar and warning that only sages could unify the realm.

sentences.zh: 司徒、琅邪王道子體道自然，神識穎遠，實當旦奭之重，宜總二南之任，可領揚州刺史、錄尚書、假節、都督中外諸軍事。

translations.literal: Minister of Education, Prince Daozi of Langye, embodies the Way in spontaneity and sees far with spirit insight; he truly bears the burden of Dan and Shi and should hold the ‘Two Souths’ charge—let him head Yangzhou, record the Masters of Writing, hold the credential, and command all military affairs within and without.”
translations.idiomatic: It named Daozi, with natural grasp of the Way and penetrating judgment, fit for the ancient weight borne by the Duke of Zhou and Shi, and charged him with Yangzhou, Masters of Writing supervision, credential, and supreme command.

sentences.zh: 衛府文武，一以配驃騎府。

translations.literal: All civil and military staff of the guard command were assigned to the grand marshal’s bureau.”
translations.idiomatic: Every officer of the guard headquarters was attached to the grand marshal’s office.

sentences.zh: 」讓不受。

translations.literal: ” He declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: ” Again he refused.

sentences.zh: 數年，領徐州刺史、太子太傅。

translations.literal: Several years later he added governor of Xuzhou and tutor to the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Years on he took Xuzhou and tutored the heir.

sentences.zh: 公卿又奏：「宜進位丞相、揚州牧、假黃鉞，羽葆鼓吹。

translations.literal: The dukes again memorialized: “He should advance to chancellor, shepherd of Yangzhou, yellow axe, plumed canopy and drum escort.”
translations.idiomatic: They pressed for chancellor, Yangzhou shepherd, yellow battle-axe, and plumed drum escort.

sentences.zh: 」並讓不受。

translations.literal: ” Together they declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: ” He turned all of it down.

sentences.zh: 于時孝武帝不親萬機，但與道子酣歌為務，姏姆尼僧，尤為親暱，並竊弄其權。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Xiaowu did not personally handle myriad affairs but made carousing with Daozi his business; wet nurses and nuns grew especially intimate and together usurped authority.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowu neglected government for drinking bouts with Daozi while nurses and nuns wormed into power.

sentences.zh: 凡所幸接，皆出自小豎。

translations.literal: Everyone he favored came from petty boys.
translations.idiomatic: Every favorite rose from low pages.

sentences.zh: 郡守長吏，多為道子所樹立。

translations.literal: Many prefects and magistrates were planted by Daozi.
translations.idiomatic: Daozi packed local posts with clients.

sentences.zh: 既為揚州總錄，勢傾天下，由是朝野奔湊。

translations.literal: Once he superintended Yangzhou and recorded the Masters of Writing, his power tilted the realm, so court and countryside flocked to him.
translations.idiomatic: Controlling Yangzhou and the Masters of Writing, he tilted the scales of power and drew every faction.

sentences.zh: 中書令王國寶性卑佞，特為道子所寵昵。

translations.literal: Palace Secretary Wang Guobao was base and sycophantic, singularly doted on by Daozi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Guobao, palace secretary, flattered shamelessly and basked in Daozi’s favor.

sentences.zh: 官以賄遷，政刑謬亂。

translations.literal: Office moved by bribes; governance and punishments ran wild.
translations.idiomatic: Posts sold for silver; law and policy collapsed.

sentences.zh: 又崇信浮屠之學，用度奢侈，下不堪命。

translations.literal: Moreover he revered Buddhist teaching, spent extravagantly, and the people could not endure the commands.
translations.idiomatic: Buddhist patronage and lavish outlays broke the commoners.

sentences.zh: 太元以後，為長夜之宴，蓬首昏目，政事多闕。

translations.literal: After Taiyuan came all-night feasts, matted hair and bleary eyes, and state business mostly neglected.
translations.idiomatic: Post-Taiyuan nights became endless revels, leaving him disheveled and half blind to duty.

sentences.zh: 桓玄嘗候道子，正遇其醉，賓客滿坐，道子張目謂人曰：「桓溫晚途欲作賊，云何？

translations.literal: Huan Xuan once waited on Daozi, found him drunk with guests packed in, and Daozi glared, saying, “Huan Wen in his late years meant to rebel—what of it?”
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan called while Daozi was sodden amid a crowd; Daozi barked whether Huan Wen’s late treason mattered.

sentences.zh: 」玄伏地流汗不得起。

translations.literal: ” Xuan collapsed to the floor streaming sweat and could not rise.
translations.idiomatic: ” Xuan fell prostrate, sweating, unable to stand.

sentences.zh: 長史謝重舉板答曰：「故宣武公黜昏登聖，功超伊霍，紛紜之議，宜裁之聽覽。

translations.literal: Senior clerk Xie Chong lifted his tablet and replied, “The late Duke Xuanwu cast down darkness and raised the sage; merit surpasses Yi Yin and Huo—noisy debate should be cut for the throne’s ears.”
translations.idiomatic: Xie Chong answered that Duke Xuanwu had deposed a dim ruler for a sage, outshining Yi and Huo, and gossip should be filtered.

sentences.zh: 」道子頷曰：「儂知儂知。

translations.literal: ” Daozi nodded, “I know, I know.”
translations.idiomatic: ” Daozi grunted, “I know, I know.”

sentences.zh: 」因舉酒屬玄，玄乃得起。

translations.literal: ” He raised a cup toward Xuan, and only then could Xuan rise.
translations.idiomatic: ” He toasted Xuan, letting him get up.

sentences.zh: 由是玄益不自安，切齒于道子。

translations.literal: From this Xuan grew less secure and ground his teeth at Daozi.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan never felt safe again and hated Daozi.

sentences.zh: 于時朝政既紊，左衛領營將軍會稽許榮上疏曰：「今台府局吏、直衛武官及僕隸婢兒取母之姓者，本臧獲之徒，無鄉邑品第，皆得命議，用為郡守縣令，並帶職在內，委事於小吏手中；

translations.literal: As court governance was already tangled, Colonel of the Left Guard Xu Rong of Kuaiji submitted: “Today bureau clerks, palace guards, and slave children who take their mothers’ surnames are originally bond-servant stock without village rank, yet all receive deliberation appointments as prefects and magistrates, holding concurrent inner posts and leaving business to petty clerks;
translations.idiomatic: Xu Rong’s memorial blasted how bond servants and nameless youths became county chiefs while real work fell to underlings.

sentences.zh: 僧尼乳母，競進親黨，又受貨賂，輒臨官領眾。

translations.literal: nuns and wet nurses push kin for place, take bribes, and then command troops.
translations.idiomatic: Nuns and nurses peddled offices and led soldiers.

sentences.zh: 無衛霍之才，而比方古人，為患一也。

translations.literal: Lacking Wei Qing or Huo Qubing’s talent yet comparing themselves to ancients is the first harm.”
translations.idiomatic: Calling such people heroes without talent was the first evil.

sentences.zh: 臣聞佛者清遠玄虛之神，以五誡為教，絕酒不淫。

translations.literal: Your servant hears the Buddha is a spirit of clarity and emptiness who teaches the five precepts, forbidding wine and lust.
translations.idiomatic: Buddha, he said, stood for purity and five renunciations.

sentences.zh: 而今之奉者，穢慢阿尼，酒色是耽，其違二矣。

translations.literal: Yet today’s devotees foul and slight nuns, drowning in wine and sex—that breaks the second precept.
translations.idiomatic: Followers instead debauched with clerics—second violation.

sentences.zh: 夫致人於死，未必手刃害之。

translations.literal: Bringing men to death need not mean wielding the blade oneself.
translations.idiomatic: Deaths need no personal knife.

sentences.zh: 若政教不均，暴濫無罪，必夭天命，其違三矣。

translations.literal: If policy and instruction are unjust, innocents die in floods of cruelty—this offends heaven, the third breach.
translations.idiomatic: Unjust rule slaughtered the guiltless, offending heaven—third breach.

sentences.zh: 盜者未必躬竊人財，江乙母失布，罪由令尹。

translations.literal: Thieves need not steal in person—when Jiang Yi’s mother lost cloth, blame lay with the chief.
translations.idiomatic: A thief need not pocket coin himself: when Jiang Yi’s mother lost her cloth, the magistrate bore the guilt.

sentences.zh: 今禁令不明，劫盜公行，其違四矣。

translations.literal: Now prohibitions are unclear and robbery walks openly—the fourth breach.
translations.idiomatic: Vague laws let banditry parade—fourth point.

sentences.zh: 在上化下，必信為本。

translations.literal: Those above transform those below; trust must be the root.
translations.idiomatic: Rule rests on credibility.

sentences.zh: 昔年下書，敕使盡規，而眾議兼集，無所採用，其違五矣。

translations.literal: Years ago an edict demanded full counsel, yet assembled opinion was ignored—the fifth breach.”
translations.idiomatic: Past orders solicited advice then ignored it—fifth breach.

sentences.zh: 尼僧成群，依傍法服。

translations.literal: Nuns swarm, clinging to clerical robes.
translations.idiomatic: Nuns mobbed the capital in robes.

sentences.zh: 誡粗法，尚不能遵，況精妙乎！

translations.literal: They cannot obey even coarse precepts, let alone subtle ones!
translations.idiomatic: They broke crude rules, never mind refined doctrine.

sentences.zh: 而流惑之徒，競加敬事，又侵漁百姓，取財為惠，亦未合佈施之道也。

translations.literal: Yet deluded folk rush to honor them, fleece the people, take wealth as kindness—this is not true giving.”
translations.idiomatic: The mob adored them while extorting alms—no charity.

sentences.zh: 」又陳「太子宜出臨東宮，克獎德業」。

translations.literal: ” He also urged that “the crown prince should move to the Eastern Palace and build virtue.”
translations.idiomatic: ” He begged the heir to enter the Eastern Palace and cultivate merit.

sentences.zh: 疏奏，並不省。

translations.literal: The memorial went up; none was heeded.
translations.idiomatic: The throne shelved it.

sentences.zh: 中書郎范甯亦深陳得失，帝由是漸不平于道子，然外每優崇之。

translations.literal: Palace Secretary Fan Ning also argued gains and losses deeply; the emperor therefore grew slowly resentful of Daozi yet outwardly continued to honor him.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Ning’s critique turned Xiaowu cool toward Daozi while publicly praising him.

sentences.zh: 國寶即寧之甥，以諂事道子，寧奏請黜之。

translations.literal: Guobao was Ning’s nephew; by fawning on Daozi he drew Ning’s impeachment.
translations.idiomatic: Guobao, Fan Ning’s nephew, served Daozi until Ning sought his ouster.

sentences.zh: 國寶懼，使陳郡袁悅之因尼妙音致書與太子母陳淑媛，說國寶忠謹，宜見親信。

translations.literal: Guobao feared and had Yuan Yuezhi of Chen command send word through the nun Miaoyin to the heir’s mother, Consort Chen, pleading Guobao’s loyalty and asking trust.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Guobao used Yuan Yuezhi and Nun Miaoyin to lobby Consort Chen for confidence.

sentences.zh: 帝因發怒，斬悅之。

translations.literal: The emperor therefore grew angry and executed Yuezhi.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowu beheaded Yuezhi in fury.

sentences.zh: 國寶甚懼，復潛甯於帝。

translations.literal: Guobao was terrified and slandered Ning to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Guobao then maligned Fan Ning to the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝不獲已，流涕出甯為豫章太守。

translations.literal: The emperor, unable to refuse, wept as he sent Ning out as governor of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Cornered, Xiaowu banished Fan Ning to Yuzhang in tears.

sentences.zh: 道子由是專恣。

translations.literal: Daozi thereafter did as he pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Daozi ruled unchecked.

sentences.zh: 嬖人趙牙出自優倡，茹千秋本錢塘捕賊吏，因賂諂進，道子以牙為魏郡太守，千秋驃騎諮議參軍。

translations.literal: Favorite Zhao Ya came from entertainers; Ru Qianqiu had been a constable in Qiantang; through bribes and flattery they advanced, and Daozi made Ya governor of Wei commandery and Qianqiu staff adviser to the grand marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ya, a performer, and Ru Qianqiu, an ex-constable, bought their way in; Daozi named Ya to Wei and Qianqiu to his staff.

sentences.zh: 牙為道子開東第，築山穿池，列樹竹木，功用钜萬。

translations.literal: Ya opened an eastern mansion for Daozi, piling hills, cutting ponds, and planting bamboo and timber at vast cost.
translations.idiomatic: Ya built Daozi an eastern villa with artificial mountains and pools.

sentences.zh: 道子使宮人為酒肆，沽賣于水側，與親昵乘船就之飲宴，以為笑樂。

translations.literal: Daozi had palace women run taverns, selling wine along the water, and he boarded boats with intimates to drink there for sport.
translations.idiomatic: Palace ladies peddled wine on the water while Daozi feasted from boats.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗幸其宅，謂道子曰：「府內有山，因得遊矚，甚善也。

translations.literal: The emperor once visited his house and told Daozi, “A hill inside the mansion lets you gaze about—very fine.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowu toured the estate, praising the interior hill.

sentences.zh: 然修飾太過，非示天下以儉。

translations.literal: Yet the ornament is excessive; it does not model thrift to the realm.”
translations.idiomatic: But the display was too rich to teach austerity.

sentences.zh: 」道子無以對，唯唯而已，左右侍臣莫敢有言。

translations.literal: ” Daozi had no reply, only assent, and attendants dared not speak.
translations.idiomatic: ” Daozi mumbled agreement; no one contradicted him.

sentences.zh: 帝還宮，道子謂牙曰：「上若知山是板築所作，爾必死矣。

translations.literal: Returning to the palace, Daozi told Ya, “If the sovereign learns the hill is rammed earth, you will die.”
translations.idiomatic: Back at court he warned Ya that exposed fakery meant death.

sentences.zh: 」牙曰：「公在，牙何敢死！

translations.literal: ” Ya said, “While you live, how dare I die!”
translations.idiomatic: ” Ya laughed, “With you above me, I cannot die.”

sentences.zh: 」營造彌甚。

translations.literal: ” Construction grew even grander.
translations.idiomatic: ” Building only swelled.

sentences.zh: 千秋賣官販爵，聚資貨累億。

translations.literal: Qianqiu sold offices and bartered noble ranks, amassing treasure in the hundreds of millions.
translations.idiomatic: Qianqiu traded posts for cash worth billions.

sentences.zh: 又道子既為皇太妃所愛，親遇同家人之禮，遂恃寵乘酒，時失禮敬。

translations.literal: Moreover Daozi, beloved of the grand imperial consort, was treated like family, so he relied on favor and wine and often broke ritual deference.
translations.idiomatic: Spoiled by the grand consort like kin, he drank his way into disrespect.

sentences.zh: 帝益不能平，然乙太妃之故，加崇禮秩。

translations.literal: The emperor grew more resentful yet, for the consort’s sake, raised her honors.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowu fumed but promoted her household out of filial duty.

sentences.zh: 博平令吳興聞人奭上疏曰：「驃騎諮議參軍茹千秋協輔宰相，起自微賤，竊弄威權，衒賣天官。

translations.literal: Magistrate Wenren Shi of Boping submitted: “Staff adviser Ru Qianqiu aids the minister, rose from the lowest dust, steals authority, and peddles heaven’s offices.”
translations.idiomatic: Wenren Shi accused Ru Qianqiu of selling seats from nothing.

sentences.zh: 其子壽齡為樂安令，贓私狼藉，畏法奔逃，竟無罪罰，傲然還縣。

translations.literal: His son Shouling is magistrate of Le’an, filthy with graft; he fled the law yet escaped punishment and swaggered back to his county.
translations.idiomatic: Ru’s son Shouling looted Le’an, fled justice, and returned unpunished.

sentences.zh: 又尼姏屬類，傾動亂時。

translations.literal: Moreover nun-kindred sway a troubled age.
translations.idiomatic: Clerical cliques rocked the times.

sentences.zh: 穀賤人饑，流殣不絕，由百姓單貧，役調深刻。

translations.literal: Grain is cheap yet people starve; corpses line the roads because commoners stand alone in poverty while corvée bites deep.
translations.idiomatic: Cheap grain and mass death came from crushing levies on the poor.

sentences.zh: 又振武將軍庾恆鳴角京邑，主簿戴良夫苦諫被囚，殆至沒命。

translations.literal: General Who Rouses Might Yu Heng sounded horns in the capital; chief clerk Dai Liangfu remonstrated bitterly and was jailed nearly to death.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Heng’s horns in the capital jailed remonstrator Dai Liangfu.

sentences.zh: 而恆以醉酒見怒，良夫以執忠廢棄。

translations.literal: Yet Heng was merely drunk-angry while Liangfu’s loyalty earned exile.
translations.idiomatic: Drunken tantrums won while honest men fell.

sentences.zh: 又權寵之臣，各開小府，施置吏佐，無益於官，有損于國。

translations.literal: Again favored ministers each open petty bureaus, appoint clerks, benefit no office, harm the state.
translations.idiomatic: Petty private offices bloated payroll without helping government.

sentences.zh: 」疏奏，帝益不平，而逼於太妃，無所廢黜，乃出王恭為兗州，殷仲堪為荊州，王珣為僕射，王雅為太子少傳，以張王室，而潛制道子也。

translations.literal: ” When the memorial arrived, the emperor grew angrier still but, pressed by the grand consort, could dismiss no one; he therefore sent Wang Gong to Yanzhou, Yin Zhongkan to Jingzhou, Wang Xun as director, and Wang Ya as junior tutor to the heir, expanding the royal house while secretly checking Daozi.
translations.idiomatic: The throne exiled Wang Gong, Yin Zhongkan, Wang Xun, and Wang Ya to strategic posts to cage Daozi.

sentences.zh: 道子復委任王緒，由是朋黨競扇，友愛道盡。

translations.literal: Daozi again trusted Wang Xu, so factions flared and brotherly love ended.
translations.idiomatic: Daozi turned to Wang Xu, sparking cliques and fratricidal hate.

sentences.zh: 太妃每和解之，而道子不能改。

translations.literal: The grand consort often mediated, yet Daozi would not change.
translations.idiomatic: She reconciled in vain.

sentences.zh: 中書郎徐邈以國之至親，唯道子而已，宜在敦穆，從容言於帝曰：「昔漢文明主，猶悔淮南；

translations.literal: Palace Gentleman Xu Miao said the state’s closest kin was only Daozi and urged harmony, telling the emperor: “Even Han Wen, a bright ruler, regretted Huainan;
translations.idiomatic: Xu Miao cited Han Wen’s regret over Huainan.

sentences.zh: 世祖聰達，負愧齊王。

translations.literal: our founder was wise yet owed Qi king apology.
translations.idiomatic: Jin’s founder still owed the Prince of Qi.

sentences.zh: 兄弟之際，實宜深慎。

translations.literal: Between brothers one must be deeply cautious.”
translations.idiomatic: Brothers demand utmost care.

sentences.zh: 」帝納之，復委任道子如初。

translations.literal: ” The emperor accepted it and entrusted Daozi as before.
translations.idiomatic: ” Xiaowu relented and restored Daozi’s power.

sentences.zh: 時有人為《雲中詩》以指斥朝廷曰：「相王沈醉，輕出教命。

translations.literal: Someone then wrote “Song of the Clouds” lampooning court: “The minister-king is drunk, tossing out orders lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Satirical verses mocked the drunk minister-king.

sentences.zh: 捕賊千秋，干豫朝政。

translations.literal: The thief-catcher Qianqiu meddles in policy.
translations.idiomatic: Qianqiu the bailiff steered policy.

sentences.zh: 王愷守常，國寶馳競。

translations.literal: Wang Kai keeps routine while Guobao scrambles for place.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Kai stays dull; Guobao claws upward.

sentences.zh: 荊州大度，散誕難名；

translations.literal: Jingzhou’s great manner—unruly beyond words;
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhou’s lord, free-spirited beyond words,

sentences.zh: 盛德之流，法護、王寧；

translations.literal: men of high virtue: Fahu and Wang Ning;
translations.idiomatic: true worthies: Fahu and Wang Ning;

sentences.zh: 仲堪、仙民，特有言詠，東山安道，執操高抗，何不徵之，以為朝匠？

translations.literal: Zhongkan and Xianmin have fine reputations; East Mountain’s Andao holds lofty integrity—why not summon them as court craftsmen?”
translations.idiomatic: Zhongkan, Xianmin, and Dai Andao should fill the halls—why not call them?”

sentences.zh: 」荊州，謂王忱也；

translations.literal: ” “Jingzhou” means Wang Chen;
translations.idiomatic: ” Jingzhou meant Wang Chen;

sentences.zh: 法護，即王殉；

translations.literal: “Fahu” is Wang Xun;
translations.idiomatic: Fahu denoted Wang Xun;

sentences.zh: 甯，即王恭；

translations.literal: “Ning” is Wang Gong;
translations.idiomatic: Ning meant Wang Gong;

sentences.zh: 仙民，即徐邈字；

translations.literal: “Xianmin” is Xu Miao’s style;
translations.idiomatic: Xianmin was Xu Miao’s courtesy name;

sentences.zh: 安道，戴逵字也。

translations.literal: “Andao” is Dai Kui’s style.
translations.idiomatic: Andao was Dai Kui’s style.

sentences.zh: 及恭帝為琅邪王，道子受封會稽國，並宣城為五萬九千戶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gong was Prince of Langye, Daozi received Kuaiji with Xuancheng, fifty-nine thousand households together.
translations.idiomatic: Gong’s princedom let Daozi hold Kuaiji plus Xuancheng at 59,000 households.

sentences.zh: 安帝踐阼，有司奏：「道子宜進位太傅、揚州牧、中書監，假黃鉞，備殊禮。

translations.literal: Emperor An’s accession brought officials’ memorial: “Daozi should advance to grand tutor, shepherd of Yangzhou, palace supervisor, yellow axe, and full extraordinary rites.”
translations.idiomatic: An’s court proposed grand tutor, Yangzhou shepherd, palace director, and yellow axe.

sentences.zh: 」固辭不拜，又解徐州。

translations.literal: ” He firmly declined and also relinquished Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: ” He refused and shed Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 詔內外眾事，動靜諮之。

translations.literal: Edicts ordered all inner and outer affairs, in motion or rest, referred to him.
translations.idiomatic: Every matter, still or urgent, was referred to him.

sentences.zh: 帝既冠，道子稽首歸政，王國寶始總國權，勢傾朝廷。

translations.literal: After the emperor’s capping, Daozi kowtowed and returned power; Wang Guobao then grasped state authority and tilted the court.
translations.idiomatic: Once An came of age Daozi feigned retirement while Guobao seized the reins.

sentences.zh: 王恭乃舉兵討之。

translations.literal: Wang Gong thereupon raised troops against him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gong marched to punish them.

sentences.zh: 道子懼，收國實付廷尉，並其徒弟琅邪內史緒悉斬之，以謝於恭，恭即罷兵。

translations.literal: Daozi feared, seized Guobao and handed him to the Minister of Justice, and executed him together with his disciple Langye administrator Xu, apologizing to Gong, whereupon Gong disbanded his army.
translations.idiomatic: Daozi sacrificed Guobao and Wang Xu to placate Wang Gong’s rebellion.

sentences.zh: 道子乞解中外都督、錄尚書以謝方嶽，詔不許。

translations.literal: Daozi begged release from commander of all armies and Masters of Writing recorder to appease the provinces; the edict refused.
translations.idiomatic: He offered to quit supreme command; the throne refused.

sentences.zh: 道子世子元顯，時年十六，為侍中，心惡恭，請道子討之。

translations.literal: Daozi’s heir apparent Yuanxian, sixteen, was palace attendant, hated Gong inwardly, and asked Daozi to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Sixteen-year-old Yuanxian, cavalier attendant, loathed Gong and urged war.

sentences.zh: 乃拜元顯為征虜將軍，其先衛府及徐州文武悉配之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yuanxian was appointed General Who Subdues the Caitiffs; the former guard headquarters and Xuzhou civil and military staffs were all assigned to him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxian became General Who Subdues the Caitiffs with the old guard bureau and Xuzhou officers placed under him.

sentences.zh: 屬道子妃薨，帝下詔曰：「會稽王妃尊賢莫二，朕義同所親。

translations.literal: It happened that Daozi’s consort died; the emperor issued an edict: “The Princess of Kuaiji ranks second to none in worth; I treat her affection as my own kin.
translations.idiomatic: Daozi’s wife died; An’s edict praised the Kuaiji princess as kin.

sentences.zh: 今葬加殊禮，一依琅邪穆太妃故事。

translations.literal: Now add extraordinary burial rites, entirely following the precedent for Grand Consort Mu of Langye.”
translations.idiomatic: Bury her with honors matching Grand Consort Mu of Langye.”

sentences.zh: 元顯夙令光懋，乃心所寄，誠孝性蒸蒸，至痛難奪。

translations.literal: Yuanxian has long shown bright virtue and is the hope of my heart; truly his filial nature steams upward, and utmost grief cannot be denied.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxian’s brilliance and grief moved the court.

sentences.zh: 然不以家事辭王事，《陽秋》之明義；

translations.literal: Yet one must not decline kingly duty for household affairs—this is the clear meaning of the Yangqiu;
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn Annals forbid shirking state for home;

sentences.zh: 不以私限違公制，中代之變禮。

translations.literal: one must not violate public regulation for private limits—this is the altered rite of middle antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: mid-era ritual barred private mourning from blocking public duty.

sentences.zh: 故閔子腰絰，山王逼屈。

translations.literal: Hence Min Zi wore hemp at the waist while the Prince of Shanyang was forced to yield.
translations.idiomatic: So Min Zi girded hemp yet the Prince of Shanyang bowed to necessity.

sentences.zh: 良以至戚由中，軌容著外，有禮無時，賢哲斯順。

translations.literal: Truly when inner kinship moves the heart, outward demeanor shows the track; where rite lacks timely leave, sages comply.
translations.idiomatic: Kinship within shapes deportment without; sages bow to ritual when timing is wrong.

sentences.zh: 須妃葬畢，可居職如故。」

translations.literal: Wait until the consort’s burial is finished, then he may hold office as before.”
translations.idiomatic: After her funeral he could resume office.”

sentences.zh: 于時王恭威振內外，道子甚懼，復引譙王尚之以為腹心。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Gong’s might shook within and without; Daozi greatly feared him and again drew in Prince Shangzhi of Qiao as confidant.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gong’s prestige terrified Daozi, who recalled Sima Shangzhi of Qiao.

sentences.zh: 尚之說道子曰：「籓伯強盛，宰相權輕，宜密樹置，以自籓衛。

translations.literal: Shangzhi told Daozi, “The provincial lords are strong while the minister’s power is light; you should secretly plant supporters to shield yourself.”
translations.idiomatic: Shangzhi urged building a private cordon against the provinces.

sentences.zh: 」道子深以為然，乃以其司馬王愉為江州刺史以備恭，與尚之等日夜謀議，以伺四方之隙。

translations.literal: ” Daozi deeply agreed, so he made his marshal Wang Yu governor of Jiangzhou to guard against Gong, plotting day and night with Shangzhi to watch for openings in the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Daozi named Wang Yu to Jiangzhou against Gong and schemed endlessly with Shangzhi.

sentences.zh: 王恭知之，復舉兵，以討尚之為名。

translations.literal: Wang Gong learned of it and again raised troops, nominally to punish Shangzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Gong rebelled again, ostensibly targeting Shangzhi.

sentences.zh: 荊州刺史殷仲堪、豫州刺史庾楷、廣州刺史桓玄並應之。

translations.literal: Jingzhou governor Yin Zhongkan, Yuzhou governor Yu Kai, and Guangzhou governor Huan Xuan all responded.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongkan, Yu Kai, and Huan Xuan joined him.

sentences.zh: 道子使人說楷曰：「本情相與，可謂斷金。

translations.literal: Daozi sent someone to persuade Kai: “Our original bond could sever metal.
translations.idiomatic: Daozi’s envoy reminded Kai of their old oath.

sentences.zh: 往年帳中之飲，結帶之言，寧可忘邪！

translations.literal: The drinking in the tent years ago, the knotted sash words—can they be forgotten!”
translations.idiomatic: How forget the camp banquet and knotted-sash pledge!”

sentences.zh: 卿今棄舊交，結新援，忘王恭疇昔陵侮之恥乎，若乃欲委體而臣之。

translations.literal: Now you abandon old allies for new friends; have you forgotten Wang Gong’s past insults, that you would bow and serve him?
translations.idiomatic: Why ditch old ties for Gong who once humiliated you?

sentences.zh: 若恭得志，以卿為反覆之人，必不相信，何富貴可保，禍敗亦旋及矣！

translations.literal: If Gong succeeds, he will deem you a turncoat and never trust you—what wealth can you keep? Disaster will follow at once!”
translations.idiomatic: Victorious Gong would call you faithless and ruin you.”

sentences.zh: 」楷怒曰：「王恭昔赴山陵，相王憂懼無計，我知事急，即勒兵而至。

translations.literal: ” Kai angrily said, “When Wang Gong once hurried to the imperial tombs, the minister-king was frantic without plan; I knew the crisis and immediately led troops.
translations.idiomatic: ” Yu Kai roared that he had saved Daozi during Gong’s earlier march on the mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 去年之事，亦俟命而奮。

translations.literal: Last year’s affair likewise saw me await command and rise.
translations.idiomatic: He had mobilized on order the year before.

sentences.zh: 我事相王，無相負者。

translations.literal: I have served the minister-king without failing him.
translations.idiomatic: He owed Daozi nothing.

sentences.zh: 既不能距恭，反殺國寶。

translations.literal: Unable to resist Gong, you instead killed Guobao.
translations.idiomatic: Daozi slew Guobao instead of facing Gong.

sentences.zh: 自爾已來，誰復敢攘袂於君之事乎！

translations.literal: Since then who has dared roll sleeves into your affairs!”
translations.idiomatic: Since then no one trusted the court!”

sentences.zh: 庾楷實不能以百口助人屠滅，當與天下同舉，誅鉏奸臣，何憂府不開，爵不至乎！

translations.literal: Yu Kai truly cannot stake a hundred kin on helping others to slaughter; I will rise with the realm, execute traitors—why fear offices and titles not coming!”
translations.idiomatic: Kai would not risk his clan for butchers; he would join the world in purging villains.

sentences.zh: 」時楷已應恭檄，正徵士馬。

translations.literal: ” At the time Kai had already answered Gong’s summons and was levying horses and men.
translations.idiomatic: Kai had answered Gong’s call and was drafting troops.

sentences.zh: 信反，朝廷憂懼，於是內外戒嚴。

translations.literal: When the messenger returned, court and capital trembled; inner and outer arms went on alert.
translations.idiomatic: His reply threw the capital into panic and general mobilization.

sentences.zh: 元顯攘袂慷慨謂道子曰：「去年不討王恭，致有今役。

translations.literal: Yuanxian, rolling up his sleeves, told Daozi fervently, “Last year we failed to punish Wang Gong, which brought today’s campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxian blamed last year’s lenience for the new war.

sentences.zh: 今若復從其欲，則太宰之禍至矣。

translations.literal: If we indulge him again, the Grand Preceptor’s calamity will arrive.”
translations.idiomatic: Another concession would doom the grand preceptor.”

sentences.zh: 」道子日飲醇酒，而委事於元顯。

translations.literal: ” Daozi drank fine wine daily and delegated affairs to Yuanxian.
translations.idiomatic: Daozi drank and left rule to his son.

sentences.zh: 元顯雖年少，而聰明多涉，志氣果銳，以安危為己任。

translations.literal: Although Yuanxian was young, he was clever and widely read, bold in spirit, and took the realm’s safety as his duty.
translations.idiomatic: Young Yuanxian was sharp, book-learned, and assumed the dynasty’s fate.

sentences.zh: 尚之為之羽翼。

translations.literal: Shangzhi was his wing.
translations.idiomatic: Shangzhi backed him.

sentences.zh: 時相傅會者，皆謂元顯有明帝神武之風。

translations.literal: Flatterers of the day all said Yuanxian had the divine martial air of Emperor Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Courtiers compared him to Emperor Ming.

sentences.zh: 於是以為征討都督、假節，統前將軍王珣、左將軍謝琰及將軍桓之才、毛泰、高素等伐恭，滅之。

translations.literal: Therefore he was made commander-in-chief of the punitive expedition with credential, leading former general Wang Xun, General of the Left Xie Yan, and generals Huan Zhicai, Mao Tai, Gao Su, and others to attack Gong and destroy him.
translations.idiomatic: He commanded Wang Xun, Xie Yan, Huan Zhicai, Mao Tai, and Gao Su to crush Gong.

sentences.zh: 既而楊佺期、桓玄、殷仲堪等復至石頭，元顯於竹裏馳還京師，遣丹陽尹王愷、鄱陽太守桓放之、新蔡內史何嗣、潁川太守溫詳、新安太守孫泰等，發京邑士庶數萬人，據石頭以距之。

translations.literal: Soon Yang Quanqi, Huan Xuan, Yin Zhongkan, and others reached Stone Citadel; Yuanxian galloped from Zhuli back to the capital, dispatching Danyang intendant Wang Kai, Poyang prefect Huan Fangzhi, Xincai administrator He Si, Yingchuan prefect Wen Xiang, Xin’an prefect Sun Tai, and others to raise tens of thousands of gentry and commoners from the capital district and hold Stone Citadel against them.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxian raced from Zhuli and massed tens of thousands at Stone Citadel against the allied rebels.

sentences.zh: 道子將出頓中堂，忽有驚馬蹂藉軍中，因而擾亂，赴江而死者甚眾。

translations.literal: Daozi was about to move out and camp at the central hall when a startled horse trampled the army, throwing it into chaos; very many drowned rushing into the river.
translations.idiomatic: Daozi’s sortie collapsed when a panicked horse stampeded troops into the river.

sentences.zh: 仲堪既知王恭敗死，狼狽西走，與桓玄屯于尋陽。

translations.literal: Once Zhongkan learned Wang Gong had been defeated and killed, he fled west in disorder with Huan Xuan and encamped at Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongkan bolted west to Xunyang with Xuan after Gong’s death.

sentences.zh: 朝廷嚴兵相距，內外騷然。

translations.literal: The court drew up stern forces opposite them; inner and outer realms seethed.
translations.idiomatic: The capital bristled with arms while the realm churned.

sentences.zh: 詔元顯甲杖百人入殿，尋加散騎常侍、中書令，又領中領軍，持節、都督如故。

translations.literal: An edict allowed Yuanxian a hundred armored guards in the hall, soon adding Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, Palace Secretary, concurrent Defender of the Center, credential, and overall command as before.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxian gained palace access with arms, then palace secretary and central command.

sentences.zh: 會道子有疾，加以昏醉，元顯知朝望去之，謀奪其權，諷天子解道子揚州、司徒，而道子不之覺元顯自以少年頓居權重，慮有譏議，於是以琅邪王領司徒，元顯自為揚州刺史。

translations.literal: When Daozi fell ill, compounded by drunken stupor, Yuanxian saw court opinion turning against him and plotted to seize his power, prompting the Son of Heaven to strip Daozi of Yangzhou and the Minister of Education—yet Daozi did not notice. Yuanxian, a youth suddenly weighty with authority, feared ridicule, so he had the Prince of Langye hold the Minister of Education while he himself took Yangzhou governor.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxian manipulated An into removing Daozi from Yangzhou and education posts, then took Yangzhou himself while Langye held the education title as cover.

sentences.zh: 既而道子酒醒，方知去職，於是大怒，而無如之何。

translations.literal: Afterward Daozi sobered, learned he had lost office, and raged without recourse.
translations.idiomatic: Sober Daozi raged helplessly.

sentences.zh: 廬江太守會稽張法順以刀筆之才，為元顯謀主，交結朋援，多樹親黨，自桓謙以下，諸貴遊皆斂衽請交。

translations.literal: Zhang Fashun of Lujiang, a man of Kuaiji, skilled with the clerk’s brush, became Yuanxian’s chief plotter, building factions and kin ties so that from Huan Qian downward every noble youth bowed to court him.
translations.idiomatic: Clerkly Zhang Fashun engineered Yuanxian’s network from Huan Qian down.

sentences.zh: 元顯性苛刻，生殺自己，法順屢諫，不納。

translations.literal: Yuanxian’s nature was harsh; life and death rested in his own whim; Fashun remonstrated repeatedly without success.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxian killed at will; Fashun’s warnings failed.

sentences.zh: 又發東土諸郡免奴為客者，號曰「樂屬」，移置京師，以充兵役，東土囂然，人不堪命，天下苦之矣。

translations.literal: He also drafted freed household slaves from the eastern commanderies into a corps called “joy dependents,” relocated them to the capital for military service; the east roared, people could not endure their orders, and the realm suffered.
translations.idiomatic: He dragooned eastern freedmen as “joy dependents” into the capital army, wrecking the lower Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 既而孫恩乘釁作亂，加道子黃鉞，元顯為中軍以討之。

translations.literal: Soon Sun En exploited the breach to rebel; Daozi was given the yellow axe and Yuanxian led the central army to punish him.
translations.idiomatic: Sun En rose; Daozi received the yellow axe while Yuanxian led the center army.

sentences.zh: 又加元顯錄尚書事。

translations.literal: Yuanxian was further added recorder of Masters of Writing affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxian also recorded the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 然道子更為長夜之飲，政無大小，一委元顯。

translations.literal: Yet Daozi returned to all-night drinking; great or small, every policy went to Yuanxian.
translations.idiomatic: Daozi drank through nights while Yuanxian decided everything.

sentences.zh: 時謂道子為東錄，元顯為西錄。

translations.literal: People called Daozi the eastern recorder and Yuanxian the western recorder.
translations.idiomatic: Wits dubbed them east and west recorders.

sentences.zh: 西府車騎填湊，東第門下可設雀羅矣。

translations.literal: The western bureau swarmed with carriages; the eastern mansion’s gate could host a sparrow net.
translations.idiomatic: Clients mobbed Yuanxian’s west office while Daozi’s east hall stood empty.

sentences.zh: 元顯無良師友，正言弗聞，諂譽日至，或以為一時英傑，或謂為風流名士，由是自謂無敵天下，故驕侈日增。

translations.literal: Yuanxian lacked good teachers or friends, heard no straight counsel, and daily received flattery—some deemed him a hero of the age, others a romantic celebrity—so he deemed himself matchless under heaven and his arrogance swelled daily.
translations.idiomatic: Praised as peerless, Yuanxian grew insufferable.

sentences.zh: 帝又以元顯有翼亮之功，加其所生母劉氏為會稽王夫人，金章紫綬。

translations.literal: The emperor also credited Yuanxian with supporting merit, raising his birth mother Lady Liu to Princess of Kuaiji with golden seal and purple ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: An ennobled Lady Liu as Kuaiji princess for Yuanxian’s service.

sentences.zh: 會洛陽覆沒，道子以山陵幽辱，上疏送章綬，請歸籓，不許。

translations.literal: When Luoyang fell, Daozi, grieving the imperial tombs’ shame, memorialized to return seals and cords and beg leave for his fief; permission was refused.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang’s loss moved Daozi to offer resignation; the throne refused.

sentences.zh: 及太皇太后崩，詔道子乘輿入殿。

translations.literal: When the grand empress dowager died, an edict ordered Daozi to enter the hall in the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Her death let Daozi ride a palace coach into the hall.

sentences.zh: 元顯因諷禮官下議，稱己德隆望重，既錄百揆，內外群僚皆應盡敬。

translations.literal: Yuanxian therefore prompted ritual officials to debate, claiming his own virtue was lofty and his prestige heavy, that having recorded the hundred bureaus, every official within and without should pay him full obeisance.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxian forced ritualists to demand universal bows to himself.

sentences.zh: 於是公卿皆拜。

translations.literal: Thereupon dukes and ministers all bowed.
translations.idiomatic: The whole bureaucracy kowtowed.

sentences.zh: 于時軍旅薦興，國用虛竭，自司徒已下，日廩七升，而元顯聚斂不已，富過帝室。

translations.literal: Armies rose one after another, state stores emptied; from the Minister of Education downward daily grain was seven sheng, yet Yuanxian’s exactions never ceased and his wealth surpassed the imperial house.
translations.idiomatic: While the court starved on seven sheng, Yuanxian hoarded beyond the throne.

sentences.zh: 及謝琰為孫恩所害，元顯求領徐州刺史，加侍中、後將軍、開府儀同三司、都督十六州諸軍事，封其子彥璋為東海王。

translations.literal: When Xie Yan fell to Sun En, Yuanxian sought concurrent Xuzhou governor, added Palace Attendant, General of the Rear, ad hoc office equal to the Three Excellencies, commander of sixteen provinces, and enfeoffed his son Yanzhang as Prince of Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: After Xie Yan’s death Yuanxian grabbed Xuzhou, rear army, sixteen provinces, and a Donghai princedom for Yanzhang.

sentences.zh: 尋以星變，元顯解錄，復加尚書令。

translations.literal: Soon because of astral omens Yuanxian relinquished recorder duties but was again named Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: A comet made him shed recorder rank yet regain director.

sentences.zh: 會孫恩至京口，元顯柵斷石頭，率兵距戰，頻不利。

translations.literal: When Sun En reached Jingkou, Yuanxian palisaded Stone Citadel, led troops to resist, and suffered repeated defeats.
translations.idiomatic: Sun En at Jingkou broke Yuanxian’s Stone Citadel defense.

sentences.zh: 道子無他謀略，唯日禱蔣侯廟為厭勝之術。

translations.literal: Daozi had no other strategy but daily prayer at the temple of Marquis Jiang for sorcerous victory.
translations.idiomatic: Daozi could only pray at Jiang Marquis’s shrine.

sentences.zh: 既而孫恩遁于北海，桓玄復據上流，致箋于道子曰：「賊造近郊，以風不得進，以雨不致火，食盡故去耳，非力屈也。

translations.literal: Soon Sun En fled to the Northern Sea; Huan Xuan again held the upper Yangzi and sent a note to Daozi: “The bandits approached the suburbs; wind stopped their advance, rain prevented fire—they left because food ran out, not because force failed.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan wrote that Sun En retreated from supply failure, not weakness.

sentences.zh: 昔國寶卒後，王恭不乘此威入統朝政，足見其心非侮於明公也，而謂之非忠。

translations.literal: After Guobao died, Wang Gong did not use that moment to seize court leadership—enough to show his heart did not insult you, yet you call him disloyal.
translations.idiomatic: Gong had spared the court after Guobao’s fall, Xuan argued.

sentences.zh: 今之貴要腹心，有時流清望者誰乎？

translations.literal: Among today’s great favorites, who ranks with the clear repute of the age?
translations.idiomatic: Who among your inner circle has real prestige?

sentences.zh: 豈可雲無佳勝，直是不能信之耳。

translations.literal: It is not that no better men exist—only that you cannot trust them.
translations.idiomatic: Better men exist but you trust none.

sentences.zh: 用理之人，然後可以信義相期；

translations.literal: Men guided by principle may then be met in good faith;
translations.idiomatic: Only the principled deserve faith;

sentences.zh: 求利之徒，豈有所惜而更委信邪？

translations.literal: profit-seekers—would they spare anything yet earn trust again?”
translations.idiomatic: mercenaries will never stay true.”

sentences.zh: 爾來一朝一夕，遂成今日之禍矣。

translations.literal: In these few mornings and evenings disaster has become today’s catastrophe.
translations.idiomatic: Thus overnight ruin arrived.

sentences.zh: 阿衡之重，言何容易，求福則立至，幹忤或致禍。

translations.literal: The weight of ‘regent’ is no light word; seek blessing and it comes at once, offend and you court ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Power like Yi Yin’s cuts both ways.

sentences.zh: 在朝君子，豈不有懷，但懼害及身耳。

translations.literal: Court gentlemen surely harbor thoughts but fear harm to themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers stay silent from fear.

sentences.zh: 玄忝任在遠，是以披寫事實。

translations.literal: Xuan, shamed to hold a distant post, therefore lays out the truth.”
translations.idiomatic: Xuan, far downstream, speaks plainly.”

sentences.zh: 」元顯覽而大懼。

translations.literal: ” Yuanxian read it and was terrified.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxian trembled at the letter.

sentences.zh: 張法順謂之曰：「桓玄承籍門資，素有豪氣，既並殷、楊，專有荊楚。

translations.literal: Zhang Fashun told him, “Huan Xuan inherits pedigree and has always been bold; having swallowed Yin and Yang, he monopolizes Jing and Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Fashun warned that Xuan owned the upper river.

sentences.zh: 然桓氏世在西籓，人或為用，而第下之所控引，止三吳耳。

translations.literal: Yet the Huans have held the western screen for generations—some will serve them—while your grip extends only over the three Wu commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan’s clan ruled the west; Yuanxian held only Wu.

sentences.zh: 孫恩為亂，東土塗地，編戶饑饉，公私不贍，玄必乘此縱其奸凶，竊用憂之。

translations.literal: Sun En’s rebellion has laid the east waste; registered households starve, public and private lack supplies—Xuan is sure to exploit this with villainy; I privately worry.”
translations.idiomatic: Sun En’s ravages and famine would let Xuan strike—Fashun feared.

sentences.zh: 」元顯曰：「為之奈何？

translations.literal: ” Yuanxian said, “What can be done?”
translations.idiomatic: ” Yuanxian asked what to do.

sentences.zh: 」法順曰：「玄始據荊州，人情未輯，方就綏撫，未遑他計。

translations.literal: ” Fashun said, “Xuan has only just taken Jingzhou; feelings are not yet settled; he is still soothing them and has no other plan.
translations.idiomatic: ” Fashun said Xuan was still consolidating Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 及其如此，發兵誅之，使劉牢之為前鋒，而第下以大軍繼進，桓玄之首必懸於麾下矣。

translations.literal: Strike now: send troops to execute him, make Liu Laozhi the van, and follow with your main host—Huan Xuan’s head will hang beneath your banner.”
translations.idiomatic: Attack at once with Laozhi as spearhead.

sentences.zh: 」元顯以為然，遣法順至京口，謀於牢之，而牢之有疑色。

translations.literal: ” Yuanxian agreed, sent Fashun to Jingkou to consult Laozhi, and Laozhi looked doubtful.
translations.idiomatic: Fashun’s mission found Laozhi hesitant.

sentences.zh: 法順還，說元顯曰：「觀牢之顏色，必貳於我，未若召入殺之。

translations.literal: Fashun returned and told Yuanxian, “Judging Laozhi’s expression, he will betray us; better summon him in and kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Fashun urged killing Laozhi preemptively.

sentences.zh: 不爾，敗人大事。

translations.literal: Otherwise he will ruin the great enterprise.”
translations.idiomatic: Else he would wreck the campaign.”

sentences.zh: 」元顯不從。

translations.literal: ” Yuanxian refused.
translations.idiomatic: ” Yuanxian declined.

sentences.zh: 道子尋拜侍中、太傅，置左右長史、司馬、從事中郎四人，崇異之儀，備盡盛典。

translations.literal: Soon Daozi was appointed Palace Attendant and Grand Tutor, with left and right senior clerks, marshals, and four retainer aides; honors were piled in full ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Daozi became grand tutor with a full retinue.

sentences.zh: 其驃騎將軍僚佐文武，即配太傅府。

translations.literal: The civil and military staff of the grand marshal’s bureau were reassigned to the grand tutor’s office.
translations.idiomatic: Grand marshal staff moved under the grand tutor.

sentences.zh: 加元顯侍中、驃騎大將軍、開府、征討大都督、十八州諸軍事、儀同三司，加黃鉞，班劍二十人，以伐桓玄，竟以牢之為前鋒。

translations.literal: Yuanxian added Palace Attendant, Grand Marshal Who Gallops as if Flying, independent office, supreme commander of the punitive expedition, military affairs of eighteen provinces, office equal to the Three Excellencies, yellow axe, twenty sword escorts, to campaign against Huan Xuan, ultimately with Laozhi as van.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxian took grand marshal, eighteen provinces, yellow axe, and Laozhi as vanguard against Xuan.

sentences.zh: 法順又言於元顯曰：「自舉大事，未有威斷，桓謙兄弟每為上流耳目，斬之，以孤荊楚之望。

translations.literal: Fashun again told Yuanxian, “Since raising this matter you have shown no stern decisiveness; Huan Qian and his brothers always serve as the upper river’s eyes—execute them to isolate Jing-Chu hopes.
translations.idiomatic: Fashun wanted Qian’s brothers killed to blind Xuan.

sentences.zh: 且事之濟不，繼在前軍，而牢之反覆，萬一有變，則禍敗立至。

translations.literal: Moreover success hinges on the van, yet Laozhi is fickle; should anything shift, disaster arrives instantly.
translations.idiomatic: Laozhi’s fickleness threatened everything.

sentences.zh: 可令牢之殺謙兄弟，以示不貳。

translations.literal: Order Laozhi to kill Qian’s brothers to prove loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Make Laozhi murder Qian’s kin to show good faith.

sentences.zh: 若不受命，當逆為其所。

translations.literal: If he disobeys, strike him first.”
translations.idiomatic: If he balks, destroy him first.”

sentences.zh: 」元顯曰：「非牢之無以當桓玄。

translations.literal: ” Yuanxian said, “Without Laozhi none can face Huan Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: ” Yuanxian insisted on Laozhi.

sentences.zh: 且始事而誅大將，人情必動，二三不可。

translations.literal: Moreover to execute a great general at the campaign’s start will shake morale—absolutely not.”
translations.idiomatic: Killing a top general at the outset would panic the army.”

sentences.zh: 」于時揚土饑虛，運漕不繼，玄斷江路，商旅遂絕。

translations.literal: ” At that time Yang land was hungry and hollow, transport failed to follow, and Xuan cut the river road so merchants vanished.
translations.idiomatic: Famine gripped Yangzhou; Xuan severed the river trade.

sentences.zh: 於是公私匱乏，士卒唯給粰橡。

translations.literal: Thus public and private were destitute; soldiers received only oak cakes and bran.
translations.idiomatic: Troops ate bran and oak meal.

sentences.zh: 大軍將發，玄從兄驃騎長史石生馳使告玄。

translations.literal: As the great host was about to march, Xuan’s cousin’s grand marshal senior clerk Shi Sheng galloped a messenger to warn Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Sheng tipped Xuan before the expedition.

sentences.zh: 玄進次尋陽，傳檄京師，罪狀元顯。

translations.literal: Xuan advanced to Xunyang, circulated a proclamation to the capital listing Yuanxian’s crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan marched to Xunyang and indicted Yuanxian.

sentences.zh: 俄而玄至西陽，帝戎服餞元顯于西池，始登舟而玄至新亭。

translations.literal: Soon Xuan reached Xiyang; the emperor in battle dress feasted Yuanxian at West Pool—he had just boarded the boat when Xuan reached Xinting.
translations.idiomatic: An armed Yuanxian at West Pool learned Xuan had hit Xinting.

sentences.zh: 元顯棄船退屯國子學堂。

translations.literal: Yuanxian abandoned the boat and withdrew to camp at the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxian fled to the national university.

sentences.zh: 明日，列陣于宣陽門外，元顯佐吏多散走。

translations.literal: The next day he drew ranks outside Xuanyang Gate; many of Yuanxian’s aides fled.
translations.idiomatic: His staff scattered before Xuanyang Gate.

sentences.zh: 或言玄已至大桁，劉牢之遂降于玄。

translations.literal: Word said Xuan had reached the Great Bridge; Liu Laozhi thereupon surrendered to Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Rumors of Xuan at the bridge made Laozhi defect.

sentences.zh: 元顯回入宣陽門，牢之參軍張暢之率眾遂之，眾潰。

translations.literal: Yuanxian raced back inside Xuanyang Gate; Laozhi’s adjutant Zhang Changzhi led troops in pursuit and the army collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Changzhi’s pursuit broke Yuanxian’s line.

sentences.zh: 元顯奔入相府，唯張法順隨之。

translations.literal: Yuanxian bolted into the ministerial mansion; only Zhang Fashun followed.
translations.idiomatic: He fled to the chancellor’s yamen with Fashun alone.

sentences.zh: 問計于道子，道子對之泣。

translations.literal: He asked Daozi for a plan; Daozi wept in reply.
translations.idiomatic: Daozi could only weep when asked for counsel.

sentences.zh: 玄遣太傅從事中郎毛泰收元顯送於新亭，縛於舫前而數之。

translations.literal: Xuan sent retainer aide Mao Tai of the grand tutor to seize Yuanxian, deliver him to Xinting, bind him before the boat, and rebuke him.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan’s officer Mao Tai dragged Yuanxian to Xinting, tied him to the prow, and denounced him.

sentences.zh: 元顯答曰：「為王誕、張法順所誤。

translations.literal: Yuanxian answered, “I was misled by Wang Dan and Zhang Fashun.”
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxian blamed Wang Dan and Zhang Fashun.

sentences.zh: 」於是送付廷尉，並其六子皆害之。

translations.literal: ” He was then sent to the Minister of Justice, and together with his six sons all were put to death.
translations.idiomatic: He and six sons went to the executioner.

sentences.zh: 玄又奏：「道子酣縱不孝，當棄市。

translations.literal: Xuan further memorialized: “Daozi is dissolute in drink and unfilial; he should be exposed in the market.”
translations.idiomatic: Xuan demanded Daozi’s public execution for debauchery and impiety.

sentences.zh: 」詔徒安成郡，使御史杜竹林防衛，竟承玄旨酖殺之，時年三十九。

translations.literal: ” An edict banished him to Ancheng commandery, ordered Censor Du Zhulin to guard him, and in the end, obeying Xuan’s intent, he was poisoned to death, aged thirty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: The court banished Daozi to Ancheng, then poisoned him at thirty-nine on Xuan’s orders.

sentences.zh: 帝三日哭於西堂。

translations.literal: The emperor wept three days in the western hall.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor An mourned three days in the western hall.

sentences.zh: 及玄敗，大將軍、武陵王遵承旨下令曰：「故太傅公阿衡二世，契闊皇家，親賢之重，地無與二。

translations.literal: When Xuan fell, the Grand General, Prince Zun of Wuling, issued order: “The late Grand Tutor served as regent across two reigns, parted and reunited with the royal house; in closeness and worth none matched him on earth.”
translations.idiomatic: After Xuan’s defeat, Prince Zun eulogized Daozi’s regency across two reigns.

sentences.zh: 驃騎大將軍內總朝維，外宣威略，志蕩世難，以甯國祚。

translations.literal: The Grand Marshal Who Gallops as if Flying ordered the court within and spread might without, aiming to sweep away the age’s troubles and settle the dynastic fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxian’s grand marshal post had held the capital and campaigned abroad to save the state.

sentences.zh: 天未靜亂，禍酷備鐘，悲動區宇，痛貫人鬼，感惟永往，心情崩隕。

translations.literal: Heaven had not quieted the turmoil; every cruelty struck together, grief moved the realm, pain pierced men and ghosts; pondering their eternal departure, hearts crumble.
translations.idiomatic: Calamity piled on calamity until the world reeled.

sentences.zh: 今皇祚反正，幽顯式敘，宜崇明國體，以述舊典。

translations.literal: Now the imperial line is restored, hidden and manifest find their order; we should exalt the national body and follow old canons.
translations.idiomatic: Restoration called for honoring the dead per precedent.

sentences.zh: 便可追崇太傅為丞相，加殊禮，一依安平獻王故事。

translations.literal: Posthumously elevate the Grand Tutor to chancellor with extraordinary rites, entirely following the precedent for Prince Xian of Ping’an.”
translations.idiomatic: Daozi was named posthumous chancellor like Prince Xian of Ping’an.

sentences.zh: 追贈驃騎為太尉，加羽葆鼓吹。

translations.literal: Posthumously award the Grand Marshal Who Gallops as if Flying as Grand Commandant, adding plumed canopy and drum escort.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxian was honored as grand commandant with plumed escort.

sentences.zh: 丞相填塋翳然，飄薄非所，須南道清通，便奉迎神柩。

translations.literal: The chancellor’s tomb mound lies neglected, buffeted and not fit; once the southern road is clear, we shall welcome the spirit bier.
translations.idiomatic: Daozi’s grave needed moving when routes cleared.

sentences.zh: 太尉宜便遷改。

translations.literal: The Grand Commandant should be promptly reburied.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxian’s remains must be relocated.

sentences.zh: 可下太史祥吉日，定宅兆。

translations.literal: Order the astrologers to choose an auspicious day and fix the tomb site.”
translations.idiomatic: Astrologers would pick a burial day.”

sentences.zh: 」於是遣通直常侍司馬珣之迎道子柩于安成。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon Acting Cavalier Attendant Sima Xunzhi was sent to welcome Daozi’s bier from Ancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Xunzhi fetched Daozi’s coffin from Ancheng.

sentences.zh: 時寇賊未平，喪不時達。

translations.literal: At the time bandits were not yet pacified, so the funeral could not arrive on schedule.
translations.idiomatic: War delayed the cortège.

sentences.zh: ，合葬于王妃陵。

translations.literal: They were jointly buried in the consort’s mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: He was laid beside Princess Wang’s tomb.

sentences.zh: 追諡元顯曰忠。

translations.literal: Yuanxian was posthumously titled Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxian received posthumous name Zhong, “the Loyal.”

sentences.zh: 以臨川王寶子修之為道子嗣，尊妃王氏為太妃。

translations.literal: Xiu, son of Prince Bao of Linchuan, was made Daozi’s heir; Consort Wang was honored grand consort.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Xiu continued Daozi’s line; Lady Wang became grand consort.

sentences.zh: 義熙中，有稱元顯子秀熙避難蠻中而至者，太妃請以為嗣，於是修之歸於別第。

translations.literal: In the Yixi era someone claiming to be Yuanxian’s son Xiuxi, fleeing among barbarians, appeared; the grand consort asked to make him heir, so Xiu returned to a side residence.
translations.idiomatic: A pretended son Xiuxi made the grand consort switch heirs until Liu Yu intervened.

sentences.zh: 劉裕意其詐而案驗之，果散騎郎滕羨奴勺藥也，竟坐棄市。

translations.literal: Liu Yu suspected deceit and investigated; it proved to be the slave Shaoyao of Gentleman Cavalier Teng Xian; they were sentenced to execution in the market.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu exposed the impostor as Teng Xian’s slave Shaoyao and had him killed publicly.

sentences.zh: 太妃不悟，哭之甚慟。

translations.literal: The grand consort did not understand and wept bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wang mourned the fraud in ignorance.

sentences.zh: 修之復為嗣。

translations.literal: Xiu again became heir.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu resumed the succession.

sentences.zh: 薨，諡悼王，無子，國除。

translations.literal: He died, posthumously titled Prince Dao, without sons; the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: He died as Prince Dao, childless, and the fief ended.

sentences.zh: 【史論】

translations.literal: 【Historian’s Commentary】
translations.idiomatic: Historian’s commentary.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：泰始之受終也，乃憲章往昔，稽古前王，廣誓山河，大開籓屏，文昭武穆，方駕于魯、衛、應、韓；

translations.literal: The chronicler says: When Taishi received the mandate, they modeled antiquity, examined former kings, swore oaths across mountains and rivers, and flung wide the screens of the provinces; civil brilliance and martial majesty were to ride paired with Lu, Wei, Ying, and Han.
translations.idiomatic: At Taishi the Jin enfeoffed princes to rival the Zhou great houses.

sentences.zh: 磐石犬牙，連衡于吳、楚、齊、代。

translations.literal: Bedrock like stone, teeth interlocking like a dog’s jaw, linked in balance with Wu, Chu, Qi, and Dai.
translations.idiomatic: The domains interlocked like the Han fiefs.

sentences.zh: 然而作法於亂，付託非才，何曾歎經國之無謀，郭欽識危亡之有兆。

translations.literal: Yet they framed law amid chaos and entrusted it to untalented men; He Zeng sighed that the state lacked strategy, Guo Qin saw omens of peril.
translations.idiomatic: But institutions born in disorder and weak princes drew He Zeng’s and Guo Qin’s warnings.

sentences.zh: 及宮車晏駕，填土未乾，國難薦臻，朝章馳廢。

translations.literal: When the palace carriage halted forever and the burial mound was not yet dry, national disasters piled up and court regulations collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Hardly was Wu Di cold when crisis shattered the statutes.

sentences.zh: 重以八王繼亂，九服沸騰，戎羯交馳，乘輿幽逼，瑤枝瓊萼，鋒鏑而消亡；

translations.literal: Compounded by the eight princes’ successive rebellion, the nine domains seethed, Rong and Jie horsemen galloped together, and the imperial carriage was driven into hiding; jade branches and carnelian calyx perished under arrowheads and blades.
translations.idiomatic: The War of the Eight Princes let barbarian cavalry pen the emperor while royal kin died in the steel.

sentences.zh: 朱芾綠車，與波塵而殄瘁。

translations.literal: Crimson ribbons and green chariots sank with the waves and dust.
translations.idiomatic: High princes drowned in the turmoil.

sentences.zh: 遂使茫茫禹跡，咸窟穴於豺狼；

translations.literal: Thus the vast traces of Yu became dens for wolves and jackals.
translations.idiomatic: The heartland became a lair for beasts.

sentences.zh: 惵惵周餘，竟沈淪於塗炭。

translations.literal: The trembling survivors of Zhou’s remnant at last sank into mud and charcoal.
translations.idiomatic: Survivors of the house fell into utter ruin.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 運極數窮，一至於此！

translations.literal: Fate exhausted and numbers ended—how could it reach this pass!
translations.idiomatic: Fortune ran out until collapse was total.

sentences.zh: 詳觀載籍，未或前聞。

translations.literal: Careful reading of the records finds no earlier hearing of such a thing.
translations.idiomatic: History shows no parallel.

sentences.zh: 道子地則親賢，任惟元輔，耽荒曲蘖，信惑讒諛。

translations.literal: Daozi stood on ground of close worth, bore the chief minister’s charge, yet drowned in mash and lees, trusted slander and flattery.
translations.idiomatic: Royal cousin Daozi led the state yet drank and heard only flatterers.

sentences.zh: 遂使尼媼竊朝權，奸邪制國命，始則彝倫攸斁，終則宗社淪亡。

translations.literal: Thereupon nuns and old women stole court power, traitors held the nation’s command; at first proper relations decayed, at last the ancestral altars fell.
translations.idiomatic: Nunnery intrigues and villains destroyed the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 元顯以童丱之年，受棟樑之寄，專制朝廷，陵蔑君親，奮庸瑣之常材，抗奸凶之臣寇，喪師殄國。

translations.literal: Yuanxian, in the years when a child’s hair is still knotted, received the burden of the state beam; he monopolized the court, slighted ruler and kin, wielded petty mediocrity, and opposed treacherous foes—losing armies and extinguishing the state.
translations.idiomatic: Boy Yuanxian seized the government, insulted the throne, and lost the realm with mediocre tools.

sentences.zh: 不亦宜乎！

translations.literal: Was it not fitting!
translations.idiomatic: Small wonder he fell!

sentences.zh: 斯則元顯為安帝之孫強，道子實晉朝之宰嚭者也。

translations.literal: Thus Yuanxian was Emperor An’s overbearing grandson, and Daozi was truly the Jin court’s Grand Pi.”
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxian was An’s tyrant grandson; Daozi played Pi to the Jin throne.

sentences.zh: 列代之崇建維城，用籓王室；

translations.literal: Past dynasties raised wall cities to screen the royal house.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier ages used princes as bulwarks.

sentences.zh: 有晉之分封子弟，實樹亂階。

translations.literal: Jin’s partition of sons truly planted the seeds of rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Jin’s enfeoffments bred rebellion instead.

sentences.zh: 《詩》云：「懷德惟甯，宗子維成。

translations.literal: The Classic of Songs says, “Cherish virtue and there is quiet; the sons of the clan are the wall.
translations.idiomatic: The Songs say virtue brings peace and princes are the wall.

sentences.zh: 無俾城壞，無獨期畏。

translations.literal: Do not let the wall crumble, lest you stand alone in dread.”
translations.idiomatic: Do not let the wall break, lest you face fear alone.”

sentences.zh: 」城既壞矣，畏也宜哉！

translations.literal: ” The wall has crumbled—how fitting the fear!
translations.idiomatic: The wall is gone—terror was inevitable.

sentences.zh: 典午之喪亂弘多，實此之由矣。

translations.literal: The many calamities of the House of Sima stemmed chiefly from this.
translations.idiomatic: Most of Jin’s ruin traced to that policy.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：帝子分封，嬰此鞠凶。

translations.literal: Encomium: Imperial sons were enfeoffed and met this crushing evil.
translations.idiomatic: Encomium: Princes were sealed and met disaster.

sentences.zh: 劄瘥繼及，禍難仍鐘。

translations.literal: Affliction heaped upon affliction; disaster struck again and again.
translations.idiomatic: Plague followed plague; catastrophe tolled on.

sentences.zh: 秦獻聰悟，清河內顧。

translations.literal: Prince Xian of Qin was keen; Prince of Qinghe looked inward.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Jian was wise; Sima Xia prudent within.

sentences.zh: 淮南忠勇，宣城識度。

translations.literal: Huainan was loyal and brave; the Prince of Xuancheng had judgment and measure.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yun was valiant; Prince Xuancheng showed foresight.

sentences.zh: 道子昏凶，遂傾國祚。

translations.literal: Daozi was dim and vicious, and so the throne toppled.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Daozi’s brutality overturned the state.
